tasks.title: checks.json gets a tier, and the gate runs the pre-merge tier
tasks.summary: Spec AC1, AC2, D6, D9, D10. `tier` on CheckCommand, validated fail-closed; absent means pre-merge; `bs gate run` runs only the pre-merge tier, records what it deferred, keeps stage-bound checks pre-merge, and refuses an empty selection; every result carries a command digest; a lock-wait timeout is recognisable as not-run.
tasks.objective: In factory/orchestrator/src/testgate.ts add `export type CheckTier = 'pre-merge' | 'post-merge' | 'pre-release'`, `export const CHECK_TIERS` (that order), optional `tier?: CheckTier` and `tierSource?: 'declared' | 'overlay' | 'default'` on CheckCommand beside `heavy` (`tierSource` is set by `readChecksFile`; task-10 adds the overlay source), `checkTier(check)` (absent -> 'pre-merge'), `selectTier(checks, tier)` (keeps file order), `declaresLaterTier(checks)` (true when any entry's tier is post-merge or pre-release), `assertCheckTier(check, file)` (throws SmithError `gate.invalid-check-tier` naming the entry, the value and the file for anything but one of the three exact strings), `commandDigest(cmd)` (sha256 hex of the raw command string), `checkDigest(check)` (sha256 hex of the canonical JSON of the entry's name, cmd, heavy and timeout_ms; never its tier; spec D5), and `isNotRun(result)` (true exactly when `reason === 'heavy.wait-timeout'`; spec D6). `run()` sets `cmd_sha256 = commandDigest(cmd)` and `check_sha256 = checkDigest(check)` on every CheckResult it returns; the command itself is never stored by this field. Call `assertCheckTier` from cli.ts `readChecksFile` beside the unchanged `heavy` and `timeout_ms` checks, and set `tierSource` to `declared` or `default`. In gate.ts export `stageBoundCheckNames(coverage?: GateCoverageOptions): string[]` (today: the coverage check name, default `coverage`). In `runGate`, before any stage runs or any event is written: when the file has at least one entry and its pre-merge selection is empty, throw `gate.no-pre-merge-checks`; when a stage-bound check's tier is later, throw `gate.stage-check-deferred` naming it (spec D9). A file with zero entries keeps today's behaviour (spec D10). Otherwise run exactly the selected checks and add to the `testgate-result` payload `tier: 'pre-merge'`, `tree_sha` (the tested worktree's `HEAD^{tree}`) and `deferred: [{name, tier, tier_source}]`. Document `tier` in usage.ts's `gate run` text.
acceptance_criteria: test/checkTiers.test.ts (write first; fails today because `assertCheckTier` does not exist): `assertCheckTier` accepts each of the three strings and absent; it refuses `"post_merge"`, `"Pre-merge"`, `""`, `null`, `1` and `true` with `gate.invalid-check-tier`, and the message names the entry and the file. `checkTier` of an entry with no `tier` is `pre-merge`; `selectTier` keeps file order; `declaresLaterTier` is false for an unlabelled file and for `[]`.

An entry with `"heavy": true, "tier": "post-merge", "timeout_ms": 600000` is accepted and `isHeavyCheck` still returns true for it; an entry with a valid tier and `"heavy": "false"` is still refused with `gate.invalid-check-heavy`.

Every CheckResult from `run` carries `cmd_sha256` equal to `commandDigest` of its command; two entries with the same name and different commands get different digests. Every result also carries `check_sha256` equal to `checkDigest` of its entry; `checkDigest` changes when the command, heavy or timeout changes and stays equal when only the tier changes.
`isNotRun` is true for the result `runHeavy` returns on a lock-wait timeout (test with an injected lock that never frees and a 1 ms wait) and false for a failed check whose command ran and exited 1.

test/gateTierFilter.test.ts: on a file of A (no tier), B (post-merge), C (pre-release), D (pre-merge), the gate runs A then D only (a fixture command appends its name to a file; afterwards it holds exactly `A`, `D`), and `testgate-result` carries `tier: 'pre-merge'`, a 40-hex `tree_sha` equal to the worktree's `HEAD^{tree}`, and `deferred` naming B and C with their tiers and `tier_source: 'declared'`.

A non-empty file whose every entry is post-merge or pre-release makes `runGate` throw `gate.no-pre-merge-checks`, and the log holds no `testgate-result` and no `gate-outcome` for that call. Under the null hypothesis (no filter guard) the same call returns pass because `run([])` passes; the test asserts the throw and the absent events, which differ from that.

A file where `coverage` carries `tier: post-merge` makes `runGate` throw `gate.stage-check-deferred` naming `coverage`, before any event; with `coverage` pre-merge the coverage-evidence stage runs as today.

An empty file `[]` passes the gate exactly as on the base (spec D10), and an unlabelled fixture yields the same check names, order, pass values and outcome as on the base; the only payload difference is `tier`, `tree_sha`, `deferred: []` and each result's `cmd_sha256`.
Every existing assertion in test/testgate.test.ts, test/gate.test.ts, test/heavyLock.test.ts and test/usage.test.ts still holds; an exact-payload assertion gains only the new fields.

It folds the task status with db/projector.ts `foldTasks`. Payload: `epic_id`, `task_ids`, `integration_branch`, `revert_sha`, `disposition` (`bounce` | `record-only`), and for `bounce`: `reverted_merge_sha`, `failing_checks`, `red_record_event_id`, `evidence_event_ids`, `log_tail`, `evidence` (`record` | `trailers-only`), `resumed`; for `record-only`: `reason` (one of `RECORD_ONLY_REASONS`), `task_ids` (the named task or `[]`), `reverted_merge_sha` (40-hex or null), and `failing_checks`, `evidence_event_ids`, `log_tail` possibly empty with `evidence: 'unreadable'`. `recordWaveReverted` refuses before writing, each with its own SmithError code: a non-40-hex `revert_sha`, a missing `integration_branch` or `disposition`, a second `wave-reverted` for the same `revert_sha`; for `bounce` also exactly one task id, a blocker from `waveRevertBlocker` (called with the `isAncestor` and `liveTaskIds` the caller passes in `opts`), an empty `failing_checks` or `evidence_event_ids`; for `record-only` a reason outside the list. Nothing else can refuse a record-only call.
acceptance_criteria: test/waveRevertedEvent.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist): `waveRevertBlocker` returns null for a completed merged task in `liveTaskIds`, and each of `not-merged`, `superseded`, `waived`, `held-by-operator` for its fixture; the same completed merged task absent from `liveTaskIds` (an amendment dropped it) returns `not-in-live-plan`, and a superseded task absent from it still returns `superseded`.

Re-merged by ancestry (a fake `isAncestor` over a small commit graph): the task's original `wave-merged` with `merge_sha` M, where M is an ancestor of R, does not make it `re-merged`; a later `wave-merged` with `merge_sha` M2, where R is an ancestor of M2, does; a `wave-merged` with no `merge_sha` never does. The mislabel case (only the original merge on the log) returns null.

`recordWaveReverted` accepts a `record-only` call for each reason in `RECORD_ONLY_REASONS`, including one with `task_ids: []`, `reverted_merge_sha: null`, empty `failing_checks`, `evidence_event_ids` and `log_tail` and `evidence: 'unreadable'`; it refuses a second record for the same `revert_sha`, a reason outside the list, and a 7-hex `revert_sha`, and the log is unchanged after each refusal.
A `bounce` call is refused for a blocker (including `not-in-live-plan`), an empty `failing_checks`, an empty `evidence_event_ids` and two task ids, each with its own code.

tasks.title: The merge queue keeps today's command, or tests the pre-merge tier when the file declares tiers
tasks.summary: Spec D2, AC3. `bs queue run --checks <file>`: an unlabelled or empty file keeps `--test-cmd`/`--select-test-cmd` exactly as today; a file declaring a later tier makes the pre-merge tier the pre-landing test; per-check results and `pre_landing` go on the queue's events.
tasks.objective: In cli.ts `queue run`, add `--checks <file>` read through `readChecksFile`. Tiers are the effective tiers `readChecksFile` returns (declared only until task-10 adds the overlay, spec D8). When `declaresLaterTier(checks)` is false (every entry pre-merge, or an empty file), nothing changes: `--test-cmd` and `--select-test-cmd` run exactly as today and the file is only validated. When it is true: the pre-landing test is `selectTier(checks, 'pre-merge')` run through `testgate.run` (short-circuit, heavy lock as `run` does) in `step` and in the `--batch` candidate (`attemptCandidate`); neither `--test-cmd` nor `--select-test-cmd` is run, and the landing event records `test_cmd_not_run: true` and, when it was given, `select_test_cmd_not_run: true` (spec D2: the flags stay accepted, so the playbook never meets `cli.invalid-flag`); an empty pre-merge selection is refused with `queue.no-pre-merge-checks`. In factory/orchestrator/src/queue.ts let StepOptions carry the optional pre-merge list. A red pre-merge run is the same blocked outcome a red test command gives today, with the failing check's tail. On the events the queue already writes for a landing and for a red pre-landing test (read queue.ts and cli.ts to find where `wave-merged` and the blocked `error-logged` are written), add `pre_landing: 'test-cmd' | 'pre-merge-tier'`, and, for the tier, the per-check results (with `cmd_sha256`) and the tested `tree_sha`. Every `wave-merged` the queue writes (step, batch and adopt; queue.ts:367, :649, :942) also carries `merge_sha`: the merge commit that landed that task on the integration branch (the per-task fold commit in `--batch`). Add it through a new taskEvents.ts export `emitWaveMergedWith(taskId, ctx, opts, filesChanged, extra)`; `emitWaveMerged` keeps its declaration and behaviour. Document the flag and the rule in usage.ts.
acceptance_criteria: test/queueTierChecks.test.ts (write first; fails today because `queue run` has no `--checks`): with an unlabelled file plus `--test-cmd` and `--select-test-cmd`, the queue runs the same commands as without `--checks` (fixture commands append their names to a file; the file and the landing event match a run without `--checks`, except the added `pre_landing: 'test-cmd'`). An empty file behaves the same way.

With a file of A (pre-merge), B (post-merge) plus `--test-cmd`, sequential `queue run --checks` runs A only, never the test command, lands the merge, and the landing event carries `pre_landing: 'pre-merge-tier'`, A's result with `cmd_sha256`, and a 40-hex `tree_sha`.
A red pre-merge check blocks the landing exactly as a red `--test-cmd` does today: nothing lands, and the blocked event carries the failing check's name and tail.
`--batch --checks` with a tiered file tests the candidate once with the pre-merge tier and lands or bisects as with `--test-cmd`.

A tiered file with `--select-test-cmd` lands as the same file without it does, running the pre-merge tier only, and the landing event says `select_test_cmd_not_run: true` (exit 0, no `cli.invalid-flag`); a tiered file with no pre-merge entry exits 1 with `queue.no-pre-merge-checks`, and nothing lands.
Every existing assertion in test/queue.test.ts and test/usage.test.ts still holds; runs without `--checks` produce the same events as on the base.

Every `wave-merged` written by step, `--batch` and adopt carries a 40-hex `merge_sha` equal to the integration-branch commit that merged that task (in `--batch`, each task's own fold commit, which `git log --first-parent` shows on the branch); `emitWaveMerged`'s existing callers and tests are unchanged.

tasks.title: Post-merge batch: the branch, the trigger, the base, a red that ran and reproduces, and the bisect
tasks.summary: Spec D4, AC6. A library that pins the integration branch, decides whether a batch is due (dependency, batch, idle and final arms), finds a digest-aware base, runs the post-merge tier at the head in a prepared scratch worktree, refuses to blame never-run, env, flaky or pre-existing reds, and bisects a reproduced red over per-task merges to name a culprit.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/postMergeBisect.ts exporting `POST_MERGE_BATCH = 4` (commented with spec D4 as its source), `assertIntegrationBranch(projectDir, epicId)` (derives the branch only through worktree.ts `integrationBranchName(epic, epicBranchPrefix(project, epic))`, requires the `<prefix>/<epic>/integration` shape and refuses the default branch from `detectDefaultBranch`, with `postmerge.not-integration-branch`), `isBsRevertCommit(message)` (true when the message carries a `Bs-Revert-Of` trailer; task-16 validates all four), `landedBsReverts(projectDir, epicId)` (spec D4's one scan: every first-parent commit from the integration branch's fork point from the default branch to the head whose message carries a `Bs-Revert-Of` trailer, oldest first, never bounded by the base) and `findPostMergeCulprit(input, ctx, opts)`. Input: epic id, project dir, the effective checks (with `check_sha256`), the plan's tasks and dependency edges, the epic's event lineage, `final`, `setupCmd`, and an injectable runner (default task-5's `runIntegrationCheck` with `workspace: 'scratch'`). Steps: (0) `assertIntegrationBranch`. (1) No post-merge entry -> `no-checks-in-tier`, nothing created. (2) Base per spec D4: the latest ancestor of the head certified (task-5's `latestTierChecks`) for every current post-merge check by `check_sha256`; else the fork point from the default branch, flagged unobserved. The head itself certified for all of them -> `no-new-merges`. (3) Unless `final`, run only when a D4 arm holds: dependency (a `todo`/`ready` plan task depends on a task merged since the base), batch (at least `POST_MERGE_BATCH` task merges since the base), idle (`inFlightTasks` names no epic task other than ones whose folded status is in `HELD_OPEN_BY_AN_OPERATOR`); else `batch-not-ready`, nothing created. (4) Run the post-merge tier at the head; setup failed -> `setup-failed`; green -> `green`. (5) Any failed result for which `isNotRun` holds -> `lock-timeout`. (6) Every failed check env-classified -> `env-failure`. (7) Re-run the failed checks at the head as a probe; any passes -> `not-reproduced`; a not-run result here -> `lock-timeout`. (8) An unobserved base is probed with the failed checks; red -> `red-at-base`. (9) First-parent commits base..head that are neither per-task merges (`Merge <task-id> into <branch>`) nor in `landedBsReverts` -> `batch-has-foreign-commit`. (10) Bisect the task merges, re-running only the failed checks at each prefix as probes (a not-run probe -> `lock-timeout`); culprit = the first merge whose prefix is red after an observed-green prefix. (11) A later merge in the batch with a plan dependency edge on the culprit -> `revert-has-dependents`. Return `culprit-found` with the culprit task id, its merge sha, the failing checks, the merges in the batch, and every record and probe event id. This module never moves a ref and never writes `wave-reverted`; task-12 does. test/helpers/integrationRepo.ts exports its repo builder so task-12 and task-16 can import it without editing it: task merges, and a bs revert commit whose four trailers are parameters (`{revertOf, task, redRecord, failingChecks}`), each defaulting to the valid value the builder derives for the merge it reverts, each replaceable by any string and each omittable, so a caller can write a non-40-hex `Bs-Revert-Of`, an unknown `Bs-Task`, an unparseable `Bs-Red-Record` or an empty `Bs-Failing-Checks`.
acceptance_criteria: test/postMergeBisect.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist), on temp repos from test/helpers/integrationRepo.ts with three task merges where merge 2 breaks a post-merge check: outcome `culprit-found`, culprit task 2, and the probe records carry `probe_of` naming the head run.

Flaky head: the post-merge check fails once at the head and passes on the re-run (fixture alternates by a counter file) -> `not-reproduced` and no culprit. Under the null hypothesis (no re-run) the same fixture names merge 3; the test asserts no culprit, which differs.

Lock: the heavy post-merge check's lock is held by another process for the head run (injected lock, 1 ms wait) -> `lock-timeout`, no probe and no culprit; held only during the bisect -> `lock-timeout`, no culprit.

Trigger: 2 merges with an epic task in flight and no dependent waiting -> `batch-not-ready` and no worktree created; the same with a `todo` task depending on merge 1 -> it runs; the same with the in-flight task `escalated` -> it runs (idle arm); `final` always runs.

Base: after a passing post-merge record at the head, editing a post-merge command (new `check_sha256`) makes the next call run instead of `no-new-merges`, and moving a check's tier does not; a new check that already fails at the fork point -> `red-at-base`, no culprit.

`landedBsReverts` finds a bs revert commit that is itself the latest certified commit (the base), and one older than the base; it ignores a hand-written commit with no `Bs-Revert-Of` trailer, and returns one whose other trailers are malformed (task-16 records it as `invalid-trailers`). Those commits come from the builder's trailer parameters: a default call writes four valid trailers, and a call overriding one trailer or omitting it writes exactly that change (asserted on the commit message).

Each other outcome has its own fixture: `no-checks-in-tier` (no record, no worktree), `setup-failed`, `env-failure` (injected gap at `SLEEP_GAP_MS`), `batch-has-foreign-commit` (a hand commit; a bs revert commit in the range is not foreign), `revert-has-dependents`.

`assertIntegrationBranch` refuses when the derived branch would be the default branch (`main`) or lacks the `/integration` shape, before any worktree is created; with every fixture, the integration ref and the clone's branch, index and tree are byte-identical before and after.

tasks.title: The check ledger: identity, duration, class and unique catches per check per run
tasks.summary: Spec D6, AC8. A pure, read-only fold over gate, queue, integration and revert events that classifies each failure as real, flaky, env or not-run, marks unique catches, severity and sensitive-path guards (failing closed on unknown tasks), and computes runs, minutes, flake rate, importance and merges per post-merge run.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/checkLedger.ts exporting `checkLedger(inputs, opts)`, a pure fold plus an injected tree-diff reader, and named constants `LEDGER_WINDOW_DAYS = 30` and `SEVERITY_WEIGHTS` (S1 8, S2 4, S3 2, S4 1), each commented with spec D6 as its source. `inputs` is task-13's `{events, taskIdOf, taskClaims, sensitiveGlobs}` (this module reads no file). Every task join goes through `taskIdOf` (event id -> qualified task id or `unattributed`). Run rows come from `testgate-result`, the queue's landing and blocked events (task-4's `pre_landing` and per-check fields), `integration-check` records (task-5's fields; probes are runs) and `wave-reverted`. Each row: identity (name plus `cmd_sha256`, or `name-only`), qualified task or epic, tiers, tree, outcome, duration from bs-gate-bounce's `environment.monotonic_ms` (absent -> `null`, never 0), class, unique or shadowed, severity, event id. Classes, unique catch, severity and the sensitive-path guard follow spec D6 exactly: a not-run result (task-1's `isNotRun`, or a name in a record's `not_run`) is counted only as `not_run`; a task that is `unattributed` or has no claims entry counts as touching a sensitive path; severity and the guard otherwise use security.ts `claimTouchesGlob` over the task's claims and `sensitiveGlobs`. The tree-diff reader defaults to `git diff --name-only --no-renames <a> <b>`; an unreadable diff makes the failure `real`. `name-only` rows count toward catches and guards, never runs or minutes. `opts.window` (`{from, to}`) applies to the numbers only; the sensitive-path guard's catch arm reads every event in `inputs`, however old (spec D6). Not-run: a check whose only failures are lock-wait timeouts has zero runs, zero minutes, zero catches and a `not_run` count equal to the timeouts; a bisect probe listing it in `not_run` adds nothing else.

Unique catch: C fails after faster F passed in the same run -> unique; C fails with faster F ordered after it (short-circuited) -> `shadowed`; F observed passing at the same tree in another record -> unique.

Severity and guard: a catch on a task claiming `src/auth/session.ts` is S1 and marks the check guarding; a check with 0 failures that ran on that task's gate inside the window is guarding too; outside the window with no catch it is not. A gate event whose `taskIdOf` entry is `unattributed`, or whose task has no claims entry, marks the check guarding (fail closed).
Identity: two rows with the same name and different `cmd_sha256` are two identities; a `name-only` real catch counts toward the guard but adds no run or minute.
A run with no `environment` has duration `null`; minutes sum measured runs only, with the unmeasured count beside them. An unreadable tree diff (injected reader throws) yields `real`.
Every number names its event ids; the fold writes nothing (inputs deep-equal before and after).

Window: a real catch on a task claiming `src/auth/session.ts` 40 days before `now`, with a 30-day window, still marks the check guarding (and task-9 then proposes nothing for it), while that catch adds nothing to the in-window runs, minutes, real catches or S1/S2 catches. tasks.objective: Edit .claude/skills/bs/wave.md: step 7 gates the pre-merge tier and keeps the rule that the unit check is the project's full test command, in whatever tier the full suite sits. Step 10 adds `--checks <file>` beside today's `--test-cmd` (and `--select-test-cmd` where used) and says the queue keeps today's command for an unlabelled file and runs neither command, without refusing either flag, once a later tier exists (spec D2); after each `bs queue run` that landed a merge, and before admitting the next tasks, it runs `bs checks post-merge` with `--project`, `--specs-dir`, `--checks`, `--plan` and `--setup-cmd` (the install command the playbook runs in task worktrees) and handles each outcome: `green`, `no-checks-in-tier`, `no-new-merges`, `batch-not-ready` move on; `reverted` logs and lets rolling admission re-admit the task; `env-failure`, `not-reproduced` and `lock-timeout` are logged (`execution.env-failure`, `execution.flaky-test`, `execution.env-failure`) and the verb is called once more, a second at the same head goes to the operator (spec OQ6); `revert-recorded` (a revert that stands without a bounce), `promotion-skipped`, `declared-tier-wins` and every other outcome go to the operator with the JSON; for `revert-not-applicable` with reason `not-in-live-plan` the playbook names the three ways out spec D4 gives (an amendment that re-adds the task, an amendment adding a task that fixes the defect, an edit to the failing check) and offers no waiver, because no verb waives a red tier. Step 9 reopens a reverted task with `bs worktree create <project> <epic> <task> --reopen --revert <revert-sha>`, puts the latest `wave-reverted`'s `failing_checks`, `log_tail` and `red_record_event_id` into the coder's brief, and counts the round on the S2 ladder. Edit .claude/skills/bs/run.md in this order (spec D5): first the playbook runs `bs checks proposals --epic <id>` with the envelope flags `--session`, `--plan-version` and `--causal-parent`, as for `bs checks apply`; only when it has items and `answered_in_epic` is false (step 12's first pass) does it ask ONE question for the whole batch, numbering items 1..n and lettering each item's options (a = keep) with their runs covered, minutes spent and minutes saved, and stating D7's reply grammar (`<n><letter>` tokens, or `none`); it turns the reply into the D7 decisions.json (a parse failure, an unknown item or letter, or a repeated item decides nothing), and runs `bs checks apply --epic <id>` exactly once, with `[]` when nothing was decided; notices are reported, not asked; silence changes nothing. Then step 12 runs `bs checks post-merge --final` and then `bs integration check --tier remaining` at the clone root. Then verdict and close, both passing `--checks`. Update .claude/agents/bs-wave-runner.md only where it restates these steps. In docs/guide/operator-guide/queue-and-gate.md §5 document `tier` beside `heavy` and `timeout_ms`, the default, the empty-file rule, the overlay (location, declared-wins, shadowed and orphaned entries), and link docs/specs/check-tiers-scope.md; in closing-an-epic.md §7a document per-tier close and `--tier remaining`. Update the scope doc's status lines to shipped. Write the CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry from the other tasks' notes.

tasks.title: Post-merge revert: build it with git revert, test and record it, land it through the queue path, bounce the task, resume
tasks.summary: Spec D1, D4, AC6. Orchestrates a post-merge batch: runs task-16's resume first, calls task-7's bisect, preflights the bounce, builds the culprit revert with `git revert -m 1` (git 2.38), tests it with the pre-merge and post-merge tiers and records those runs at the revert commit, lands it through queue.ts landCandidate on the pinned integration branch, then writes wave-reverted.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/postMerge.ts exporting `runPostMerge(input, ctx, opts)`. `liveTaskIds` are the ids of the input plan's records whose `task_status` is not `superseded` (the plan `bs checks post-merge --plan` read, the file `bs wave next` reads). (0) Call task-7's `assertIntegrationBranch`, then task-16's `resumeLandedReverts` with `liveTaskIds`; when it wrote anything, return its outcome and `resumed: true`. The result shape is `{outcome, resumed, reason?, culprits, revert_sha?, event_ids}`. `culprits` is a list of `{task, merge_sha, failing_checks, red_record_event_id, reproduced: true}`: on every outcome reached after task-7 returned `culprit-found` it holds that one culprit; on a resumed return (step 0) it holds the `culprit` of each resumed write that has one (task-16, rebuilt from the trailers); otherwise it is empty. task-14 promotes on every entry (spec D7), so a check whose catch was recorded by a resume after a crash is promoted like any other. (1) Call task-7's `findPostMergeCulprit`; return its outcome unchanged for anything but `culprit-found`. (2) Preflight: `waveRevertBlocker` for the culprit with `liveTaskIds`; a reason -> `revert-not-applicable` with that `reason` on the result, nothing built. For `not-in-live-plan` (a plan amendment dropped the finished culprit before this batch ran) nothing is reverted: the culprit's change stays on the integration branch, the head stays uncertified so close keeps refusing, and the outcome goes to the operator once with the culprit, the failing checks and the red record. The answer is one of three things, each of which re-certifies the head: a plan amendment that re-adds the task (plan.ts `draftNextVersion` accepts an added id the previous version does not hold live, so the next batch reverts and bounces it), a plan amendment adding a task that fixes the defect, or an edit to the failing check. No verb waives a red tier, so none is offered (spec D4). (3) Build: in a scratch worktree detached at the head (same `.wt/<project>/` root, removed in a `finally`), `git revert -m 1 --no-edit <culprit-merge>` then amend the message to carry the four trailers (`Bs-Revert-Of`, `Bs-Task`, `Bs-Red-Record`, `Bs-Failing-Checks`); a conflict is aborted (`git revert --abort`) -> `revert-conflict`. (4) Test the revert commit R with the pre-merge tier and then the whole post-merge tier through `runIntegrationCheck` with `workspace: 'scratch'`, `commit: R` and the current digest, writing both as certifying records at R; a not-run result -> `lock-timeout`; setup failure -> `setup-failed`; any other red -> `revert-red`. (5) Land R with queue.ts `landCandidate(projectDir, integrationBranch, head, R, message)`, where `integrationBranch` comes only from the branch `assertIntegrationBranch` returned; `landCandidate` is exported from queue.ts by this task without other change; `integration-dirty` and `integration-moved` are returned and nothing else is written. (6) After `landed`, `recordWaveReverted` (`disposition: bounce`) with the failing checks, the log tail, the red record id and every record and probe id -> `reverted`. A refusal or crash here is finished by task-16's resume on the next call. Only `reverted` writes `wave-reverted`; every other outcome moves no ref.
acceptance_criteria: test/postMergeRevert.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist), on task-7's fixture repos with three task merges where merge 2 breaks a post-merge check and no worktree holds the integration branch: outcome `reverted`; the ref points at a new commit whose parent is the old head, whose tree equals the old head without merge 2's change and whose message carries the four trailers; passing pre-merge and post-merge records exist at the new head and no further whole-tier run happened after the landing (fixture counter); one `wave-reverted` names task 2 with the probe ids.

With a clean worktree holding the integration branch (the clone or an epic worktree), `reverted` fast-forwards that worktree: its HEAD equals the new ref and `git status --porcelain` is empty. With tracked changes in the holder, the outcome is `integration-dirty`, the ref is unchanged and no `wave-reverted` exists.

Crash after landing: an injected throw right after `landCandidate` leaves the ref moved and no `wave-reverted`; the next `runPostMerge` call returns `{outcome: 'reverted', resumed: true}` (task-16's result passed through) with `culprits` holding task 2's culprit rebuilt from the trailers, exactly one `wave-reverted`, and a third call proceeds to the normal flow.

A revert that breaks a pre-merge check only (the culprit's export is imported by a later file; a pre-merge typecheck-like check fails after the revert) -> `revert-red`, ref unchanged. A revert conflict -> `revert-conflict`, ref unchanged, no revert in progress left in any worktree. A ref moved while R is tested -> `integration-moved`, ref left where the mover put it. A lock-wait timeout in R's test -> `lock-timeout`, ref unchanged.

Pinned branch: with the epic's prefix configured so the derived branch would be the default branch, `runPostMerge` throws `postmerge.not-integration-branch` before any worktree is created, and `main` is unchanged.

The mechanism runs on git 2.38: the module uses no `merge-tree --merge-base` (a grep criterion over the diff) and the test uses only `git revert`, `worktree`, `rev-parse`, `log` and `update-ref` via `landCandidate`.
`landCandidate` is exported from queue.ts with its declaration unchanged, and every existing assertion in test/queue.test.ts still holds.

`culprits` holds exactly one culprit, naming the task and failing checks, on `reverted`, `revert-has-dependents`, `revert-not-applicable`, `revert-conflict`, `revert-red`, `integration-dirty`, `integration-moved`, and on `setup-failed` and `lock-timeout` raised while R is tested (one fixture each: the setup command fails in R's scratch worktree; R's heavy check finds the lock held, 1 ms wait), and is empty on `green`, `not-reproduced`, `env-failure`, `red-at-base`, and on `setup-failed` and `lock-timeout` before a culprit (the head run's own setup failure or lock wait); the revert commit's message carries all four trailers.

Amended away (spec D4), fixture in this order: merge tasks 1-3 where merge 2 breaks a post-merge check; then a plan amendment drops the finished task 2 (the plan input is a v2 that omits it, as `draftNextVersion` does, with `plan-version-created` on the log); then `runPostMerge` -> `revert-not-applicable` with `reason: 'not-in-live-plan'` and task 2's culprit, no scratch worktree created, the integration ref unchanged and no `wave-reverted` on the log. Without the amendment (the v1 plan input with task 2 live, and no `plan-version-created` for v2) the same repo gives `reverted`, so the two runs differ only by the amendment. Re-adding task 2 by a v3 amendment (its id in `liveTaskIds` again) makes the next call `reverted`, so the first way out the operator is offered works.

Diff check (AC13), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff --no-renames <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout (for example a `timeout_ms` line that only validates or passes through an existing value). An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

functional_clauses: Nothing lands untested: the exact revert commit is tested with the pre-merge and post-merge tiers, and recorded, before the ref moves.
The ref moves only through `landCandidate` on the branch `assertIntegrationBranch` returned; no checkout, reset, rebase or force of any branch, and a dirty holder is never written into.
No state in which a revert landed and the log keeps no record of it after the next call: step 0 is task-16's resume.
One culprit per run; a red revert lands nothing.
`wave-reverted` only through task-2's `recordWaveReverted`.

tasks.title: Ledger inputs: one project's events across lineages, qualified task ids, and the claims map
tasks.summary: Spec D6, AC8. A reader that gathers every session log for the epics under one specs dir across lineages, returns every kept event with the window bounds (no time filter; task-8 windows the numbers), keeps unattributed events, qualifies every task id, builds the task-to-claims map and sensitive globs, skips unreadable plans with a warning, and marks the result degraded on an unreadable session log.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/ledgerInputs.ts exporting `gatherLedgerInputs({stateDir, specsDir, sensitivePathsFile, now, windowDays})`. Layout: `specsDir` is the parent directory holding `<epic>/plan.json` and `<epic>/plan-v<n>.json`, as `--specs-dir` is on every existing verb. Epics: every `<epic>` directory there. Plans: the reader needs only `project`, `tasks`, and each task's `task_id` and `claims`; a plan file that does not parse or lacks those is skipped with a warning `{code: 'checks.plan-skipped', path, reason}` (no full plan validation). The project scope is the `project` of the readable plans; more than one distinct value throws `checks.mixed-projects`; no readable plan at all throws `checks.no-plans`. Events: every session in `stateDir` (events.ts `listSessionIds`, `readEvents`, `mergeSessionLogs`); a session `readEvents` cannot read adds `{code: 'checks.session-unreadable', path}` to the warnings and sets `degraded: true`. Keep an event when its epic (qualified `task_id`, `payload.epic_id`, or its session's single epic) is one of the epics, or when its session's lineage touches one of them. Do not filter by time: return `window: {from: now - windowDays, to: now}` beside the events, and task-8 applies it to the numbers only (spec D6). Qualify every kept event's task id with taskId.ts (`epicOfTaskId`, `qualifyTaskId`, `taskIdsMatch`): a qualified id as is; a bare id with its session's epic when the session or its lineage names exactly one epic; else `unattributed` (kept, never dropped). Claims: per qualified task id, the claims of its latest spec across the readable plan files, plus `task-added` records for follow-ups; a skipped plan's tasks get no entry, so task-8 counts them as sensitive. Sensitive globs: `loadSensitivePathsPolicy`. Returns `{events, window, taskIdOf, taskClaims, sensitiveGlobs, epics, project, sessionsRead, warnings, degraded}`. Read-only.
acceptance_criteria: test/ledgerInputs.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist): a fixture state dir with three sessions (two epics under the specs dir across two lineages, one epic elsewhere) yields every event of the two epics, in or out of the window, and none of the third, and `sessionsRead` is 3.

Task ids: a `testgate-result` with `task_id: "task-3"` in a session of epic E and one with `"E/task-3"` both map to `E/task-3` in `taskIdOf` and find the same claims; a bare id in a session whose lineage names two epics of the project is present in `events` and maps to `unattributed` (and, through task-8, marks the check guarding).

Events 31 and 400 days before `now` are both returned, and `window` is `[now - 30 days, now]` for a 30-day window. `taskClaims` takes a task's claims from its latest plan version, and a follow-up's from its `task-added` record.

A truncated plan file, and an old-schema plan missing a field the reader does not need, are handled differently: the truncated one is skipped with a `checks.plan-skipped` warning naming its path and its epic's events are still kept with no claims entries; the old-schema one is read. Plans naming two projects throw `checks.mixed-projects`; a specs dir with no readable plan throws `checks.no-plans`.
A session log with a non-JSON line yields `degraded: true` and a `checks.session-unreadable` warning naming the file; the other sessions' events are still returned.
Nothing in the state dir or specs dir changes (file mtimes and contents identical before and after).

Diff check (AC13), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff --no-renames <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout (for example a `timeout_ms` line that only validates or passes through an existing value). An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

Every task id is qualified before it leaves this module; an id that cannot be qualified is `unattributed`, never dropped.

tasks.title: The `bs checks post-merge` verb, tiered integration check, close with a checks file, and reopen
tasks.summary: Spec AC4-AC7, AC10, AC12. Ships `bs checks post-merge` (with automatic promotion, using the namespace-wide flags), `integration check --tier <tier|all|remaining>`, `epic close|verdict --checks`, and `worktree create --reopen --revert`.
tasks.objective: In cli.ts and usage.ts: (1) `bs checks post-merge --epic <id> --project <dir> --checks <file> --plan <plan.json> [--setup-cmd <cmd>] [--final] [--state-dir <dir>] [--now <iso>] --session <id> --plan-version <n> --causal-parent <event-id>` (flags mean what they mean in task-10) calls task-12's `runPostMerge` with the plan's tasks and edges and the effective checks, prints one JSON document with the outcome (and its `reason` when task-12 gives one), and exits 0 only for `green`, `reverted`, `no-checks-in-tier`, `no-new-merges` and `batch-not-ready`, else 1 (`revert-recorded` included, so the operator hears of it once). For every entry in task-12's `culprits` (every outcome reached after the culprit is found, and a resumed write's culprit rebuilt from its trailers, spec D7), it calls task-9's `promoteAfterCatch` with that culprit for each failing check, and adds the promotions, `declared-tier-wins`, or `promotion-skipped` with the reason (an overlay refusal such as `checks.overlay-tracked` or `checks.overlay-busy`) to the JSON; promotion needs no ledger, and a promotion failure never changes the post-merge outcome or its exit code. The JSON also carries task-15's overlay report. (2) `bs integration check --tier <pre-merge|post-merge|pre-release|all|remaining>` passes the tier. tasks.summary: Spec D8, AC9, AC10. tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/tierOverlay.ts exporting: `overlayPath(dir)` (the main worktree of the repository holding `dir`, from `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, then `.blacksmith/check-tiers.json`; `withOverlayLock(dir, fn, opts)` (never called when `overlayPath(dir)` is null: every caller, task-9's apply and promotion and task-10's proposals, checks first and answers `not-a-repo` without locking, and a call made anyway throws `checks.overlay-not-a-repo` before creating anything; `writeOverlay(dir, {entries, expectedRevision}, opts)` (must run inside the lock; refuses `checks.overlay-not-a-repo`, `checks.overlay-tracked`, `checks.overlay-unreadable`, and `checks.overlay-moved` when the file's revision is not `expectedRevision`; `resolveEffectiveTiers(checks, overlay)` (per entry: declared `tier` -> `declared`; else an overlay entry with the same name and `commandDigest(cmd)` -> `overlay`; else `pre-merge`/`default`; an unreadable or absent overlay resolves every undeclared entry to `pre-merge`/`default`); `overlayReport(checks, overlay)` (spec D8's precedence: no entry with that name -> `orphaned`; that entry declares a tier -> `shadowed`, also when its command changed; digest differs -> `orphaned`; else `active`); `overlayOwes(overlay, events)` (pure: the approved `check-tier-decided` and `check-tier-promoted` tiers the overlay lacks and the `pending_event`s still owed; empty for an absent overlay when the log holds no approved decision); and `reconcileOverlay(dir, events, ctx, opts)` (inside the lock, re-reading the overlay there and writing exactly what `overlayOwes` reports: entries the approved `check-tier-decided` and `check-tier-promoted` events imply but the overlay lacks are written; a `pending_event` still owed is appended through `appendEvent` exactly as stored and cleared; nothing else changes). An entry's `pending_event`, when present, is an object with exactly `event_type` (the string `check-tier-promoted`) and an object `payload`; anything else makes the overlay unreadable. tierOverlay.ts writes no event type of its own: it recognises `check-tier-decided` and `check-tier-promoted` by comparing `event_type` strings and appends only the stored `pending_event`, so no `event_type:` property in it names a literal or constant, and it adds nothing to taxonomy.yml (task-9, which writes the three `check-tier-*` names, declares them).

A valid file reads back deep-equal.

Report precedence: for one overlay entry `e2e`, the check absent from the file -> `orphaned`; present and declaring a tier -> `shadowed`, also with its command edited; present, undeclared, command edited -> `orphaned`; present, undeclared, same command -> `active`, and `resolveEffectiveTiers` gives it the overlay tier with source `overlay`.

The project's checks file is never written: every exported function run against a temp repo whose checks file is mode 0444 leaves that file's bytes and mtime unchanged and raises no permission error.

tasks.summary: Spec D4, AC6. Scans the integration branch from its fork point for bs revert commits with no `wave-reverted`, validates their trailers, and finishes each: a bounce when the task is still completed and not re-merged, a record-only event with a listed reason otherwise, always accepted; no outcome repeats.

Input: project dir, epic id, the integration branch from task-7's `assertIntegrationBranch`, the epic's event lineage, and `liveTaskIds` (task-12 passes them: the live plan's records whose `task_status` is not `superseded`). For each commit task-7's `landedBsReverts` returns (fork point to head, oldest first) with no `wave-reverted` naming its sha: validate the trailers per spec D4 (`Bs-Revert-Of` 40-hex and a merge commit on the branch's first-parent history; `Bs-Task` a task id of this epic, qualified or bare, qualified with taskId.ts; `Bs-Red-Record` an event id `parseEventId` accepts; `Bs-Failing-Checks` a non-empty comma list). Invalid trailers -> `record-only` with reason `invalid-trailers`; a task id the lineage does not know -> `unknown-task`. Otherwise call task-2's `waveRevertBlocker` with `revertSha`, a git `isAncestor` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) and `liveTaskIds`: null -> `recordWaveReverted` with `disposition: bounce`, `resumed: true`, `failing_checks` from the trailer, the log tail and evidence ids from the red record when it can be read (`evidence: 'record'`), else the trailer's checks and the red record id only (`evidence: 'trailers-only'`); a reason -> `record-only` with that reason and whatever evidence can be read (`evidence: 'unreadable'` with empty lists when none). Each write whose trailers are valid and whose task is known and merged (every reason except `invalid-trailers`, `unknown-task` and `not-merged`) also yields `culprit`, rebuilt from the trailers in task-12's shape: `{task: <Bs-Task, qualified>, merge_sha: <Bs-Revert-Of>, failing_checks: <Bs-Failing-Checks>, red_record_event_id: <Bs-Red-Record>, reproduced: true}`. `reproduced: true` holds because task-12 builds a bs revert commit only after task-7 returned `culprit-found` (spec D4); whether each check's own failure was env or not-run is read later from the red record by task-9's promotion, never assumed here. Return `{outcome, resumed, wrote: [{task, revert_sha, disposition, reason?, culprit?}]}`: outcome `reverted` with `resumed: true` when every write was a bounce, `revert-recorded` when any was record-only, `nothing-to-resume` (`resumed: false`) when none was missing. It never moves a ref. Its fixtures are built inside test/postMergeResume.test.ts with the repo builder task-7 exports from test/helpers/integrationRepo.ts (imported, not edited).
acceptance_criteria: test/postMergeResume.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist), with a bs revert commit landed and no `wave-reverted`: the task still completed -> one `wave-reverted` with `disposition: bounce`, return `{outcome: 'reverted', resumed: true}`, and the task folds to `todo`.

One fixture per record-only exit, each writing exactly one `record-only` event with the named reason, returning `revert-recorded`, and leaving the task's folded status unchanged: superseded after the revert; waived; escalated (`held-by-operator`); merged again after the revert, by a `wave-merged` whose `merge_sha` has R as an ancestor (`re-merged`); a `Bs-Task` naming no known task (`unknown-task`); a `Bs-Task` naming a task the lineage knows (its `wave-admitted`) with no `wave-merged` (`not-merged`); a task merged and still completed that a later plan amendment dropped, so `liveTaskIds` lacks it (`not-in-live-plan`); a `Bs-Revert-Of` that is not 40-hex (`invalid-trailers`). Every bad trailer value is written through the trailer parameters of task-7's builder, never by a hand-made commit.
Mislabel guard: the task's original `wave-merged` carries the `merge_sha` R reverts; the resume writes a `bounce`, never `re-merged`.

Unreadable evidence: with the red record named by `Bs-Red-Record` absent from the log, a bounceable task gets a `bounce` with `evidence: 'trailers-only'` and `failing_checks` from the trailer; a superseded one gets a `record-only` with `evidence: 'unreadable'`; neither write is refused.

No repetition: after any exit, a second call returns `nothing-to-resume` and writes nothing. A bs revert commit that is itself the latest certified commit, and one older than the base, are both found.
The integration ref and the clone's branch, index and tree are byte-identical before and after every fixture.

tasks.title: A bounced revert reopens the task everywhere the lifecycle is read
tasks.summary: Spec D1, AC7. The projector, finishedInLog and reinstatementBlocker treat a `bounce` wave-reverted as no merge, so goal-check, amend, readiness, wave next and admission all see the task as open; `record-only` changes nothing.
tasks.objective: A task is reverted when its latest `wave-merged` is followed by a `wave-reverted` with `disposition: 'bounce'` naming it (match the event type and payload by their strings, as the projector's other arms do, so this task imports nothing from task-2's revert.ts); a `record-only` event never reopens anything. Apply that rule in: db/projector.ts `foldTasks` (`completed` -> `todo`, clearing whatever terminal bookkeeping a later `wave-merged` needs; read schema.ts's `terminalAt` comment and keep its rule; other statuses untouched); taskLifecycle.ts `finishedInLog` (a reverted task is not finished, so `creditableTaskIds`, `markFinishedFromLog`/`draftNextVersion`, specChange.ts and spec.ts all see it open without edits of their own) and `reinstatementBlocker` (a reverted merge is no merge). Change waveNext.ts or admission.ts only where a test shows the reverted row is not offered or admitted. A task the live plan no longer holds is never bounced: a plan amendment drops a finished task from v(n+1) (plan.ts `draftNextVersion`), so task-2's `waveRevertBlocker` returns `not-in-live-plan` for it, task-12 builds no revert, and task-16 records an already-landed one `record-only` (spec D4). Every `bounce` this task reads therefore names a task the live plan holds, and it needs no way back for a dropped one. The new arm makes `projectTasks` compare one more event type, so add `'wave-reverted'` to db/foldPredicates.ts `TASK_TYPES`: test/db/foldPredicates.test.ts walks `projectTasks` and every function it calls and fails any compared type the tasks predicate rejects on an empty payload. Compare against a string literal or a module-level `const` so that guard can resolve the operand, and change nothing else in foldPredicates.ts (its only importer is projector.ts, which this task also claims; no other task claims either file).
acceptance_criteria: test/waveReverted.test.ts (write first; fails today because the projector ignores `wave-reverted` and the row stays `completed`): after `wave-merged` then a `bounce` `wave-reverted` for task T (raw events in the fixture), `foldTasks` gives T `todo`; a second `wave-merged` gives `completed` again.

After the bounce: `finishedInLog` omits T; `creditableTaskIds` does not credit T; `markFinishedFromLog` then `draftNextVersion` keeps T live (not completed, not dropped) in the drafted next version; the epic readiness check lists T as not terminal-OK; `computeNextWave` with the log's status map offers T; `inFlightTasks` does not count T in flight. After a second `wave-merged` each of these reads T as finished again.

A `record-only` `wave-reverted` for a completed task and for a superseded task changes none of these readers. Nor does one with `reason: 'not-in-live-plan'`, in this order: `wave-merged` for T, a `plan-version-created` whose v2 omits T (as `draftNextVersion` drafts it), then the `record-only` event; `finishedInLog` still lists T, `creditableTaskIds` still credits it through its earlier-version rule, and `draftNextVersion` of v2 does not bring T back.

New module factory/orchestrator/src/revert.ts exporting `WAVE_REVERTED_EVENT`, `RECORD_ONLY_REASONS = ['superseded', 'waived', 'held-by-operator', 're-merged', 'not-merged', 'not-in-live-plan', 'unknown-task', 'invalid-trailers']` (the one list task-16 uses), `waveRevertBlocker(events, taskId, epicId, {revertSha, isAncestor, liveTaskIds})` and `recordWaveReverted(input, ctx, opts)`, the only writer of the event. `waveRevertBlocker` is pure with an injected `isAncestor(a, b)`; it returns null, or the first reason that holds: `not-merged` (no `wave-merged` names the task), `superseded`, `waived`, `held-by-operator` (`failed` or `escalated`), `re-merged` (some `wave-merged` for the task carries a `merge_sha` that has `revertSha` as an ancestor; a `wave-merged` without `merge_sha` never counts, spec D4), `not-in-live-plan` (no id in `liveTaskIds` matches the task by taskId.ts `taskIdsMatch`; `liveTaskIds` is the ids of the live plan's records whose `task_status` is not `superseded`, read by the caller from the same plan file `bs wave next` reads, because a plan amendment drops a finished task from v(n+1) (plan.ts `draftNextVersion`) and a bounce could then reopen it only in the projector, spec D4). It folds the task status with db/projector.ts `foldTasks`. Payload: `epic_id`, `task_ids`, `integration_branch`, `revert_sha`, `disposition` (`bounce` | `record-only`), and for `bounce`: `reverted_merge_sha`, `failing_checks`, `red_record_event_id`, `evidence_event_ids`, `log_tail`, `evidence` (`record` | `trailers-only`), `resumed`; for `record-only`: `reason` (one of `RECORD_ONLY_REASONS`), `task_ids` (the named task or `[]`), `reverted_merge_sha` (40-hex or null), and `failing_checks`, `evidence_event_ids`, `log_tail` possibly empty with `evidence: 'unreadable'`. `recordWaveReverted` refuses before writing, each with its own SmithError code: a non-40-hex `revert_sha`, a missing `integration_branch` or `disposition`, a second `wave-reverted` for the same `revert_sha`; for `bounce` also exactly one task id, a blocker from `waveRevertBlocker` (called with the `isAncestor` and `liveTaskIds` the caller passes in `opts`), an empty `failing_checks` or `evidence_event_ids`; for `record-only` a reason outside the list. tasks.objective: In cli.ts `queue run`, add `--checks <file>` read through `readChecksFile`. tasks.title: Integration runs by tier, a prepared scratch runner, and one certification rule
tasks.summary: Spec D3, D5, AC4. `runIntegrationCheck` runs a tier, `all` or `remaining` at the clone root under today's contract, or at any commit in a prepared, always-removed scratch worktree, and every record names the commit it ran at, its tiers, digests, tree, not-run checks and per-check `environment`; `certifyChecks` is the one definition of a check certified at a commit, read by `remaining`, the close (task-6) and the bisect base (task-7).
tasks.objective: In factory/orchestrator/src/integration.ts add optional `tier` (`CheckTier | 'all' | 'remaining'`), `workspace` (`'clone' | 'scratch'`, default `'clone'`), `commit` (`string`), `setupCmd` (`string`), `probeOf` (`string`) and `environmentSources` (`EnvironmentSources`, passed to `run` exactly as `runGate` passes it, so tests inject the clocks) to `IntegrationCheckInput`. `latestIntegrationCheck` is unchanged, byte for byte. Where a run happens. `workspace: 'clone'` keeps today's contract, refusals and their order (`integration.no-checks`, `integration.branch-missing`, `integration.not-a-repo`, `integration.wrong-branch`, `integration.dirty-tree`). `workspace: 'scratch'` is for task-7 and task-12; the CLI never sets it. It requires `commit`; `commit` and `setupCmd` are accepted only with `workspace: 'scratch'`; and `probeOf`, when given, must be a non-empty string. Each violation throws `integration.bad-input` naming the field, before anything runs or is written. The commit is resolved in the clone with `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <commit>^{commit}`; an unresolvable one throws `integration.unknown-commit`. `integration.branch-missing` still applies to a scratch run; `integration.wrong-branch` and `integration.dirty-tree` do not, because a scratch run never reads or changes the clone's branch, index or tree. A scratch run executes the checks through `runChecksAt` at the resolved sha, passing `setupCmd`, `timeoutMs`, `runAll` and `environmentSources` through. When `runChecksAt` returns `setupFailed`, `runIntegrationCheck` writes no record and throws `IntegrationCheckError` with code `integration.setup-failed`, whose details carry `epicId`, `commit` (the resolved sha), `setup` and `deps` from the `RunChecksAtResult`. A failed setup or deps block is therefore never a record, never a pass and never a red, and task-7 and task-12 map exactly this code to their `setup-failed` outcome (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-ead87064). Which commit a record names (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-a5a7af62). A run's target commit is the integration branch head for a clone run and the resolved `commit` for a scratch run. The record's `head_sha` is that full 40-hex sha, its `tree_sha` is that commit's tree (`git rev-parse <sha>^{tree}`), and its `branch` is the epic's integration branch name exactly as main computes it (`integrationBranchName(epic, epicBranchPrefix(project, epic))`), for a scratch run too. So a scratch record at a commit that is not on the branch yet, such as task-12's revert candidate R, is filed under R and certifies R once R lands (queue.ts `landCandidate` fast-forwards the branch to the candidate, so the landed head is R itself). What a run selects. Without `tier`, every check, as today. A tier selects that tier (task-1's `selectTier`); `all` selects every check; `remaining` selects every check for which `certifyChecks` (below) returns `certified: false` at the target commit, each queried by its name and task-1's `checkDigest(check)`, over the events `readLineageEvents(ctx.sessionId, opts)` returns, read once; the same definition the close applies, so a check `remaining` skips is one the close counts as certified (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9f20e9f0). An empty selection writes no record and throws: `integration.nothing-remaining`, naming the target commit, when `tier` is `remaining` and the input checks are not empty (every check is already certified there, which run.md step 12 treats as done, task-11); `integration.no-checks`, naming the tier, in every other case (spec D10) (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-059cacdc). What a record carries. Every `integration-check` record this task writes keeps main's `epic_id`, `branch`, `head_sha`, `pass` and `results` (each result now carrying task-1's `cmd_sha256` and `check_sha256`), and gains: `tiers` (the tiers of the checks it ran, in `CHECK_TIERS` order; a run without `tier` lists every tier present); `tiers_present` (the tiers of all the input checks, in `CHECK_TIERS` order); `tree_sha`; `not_run` (the names of results for which task-1's `isNotRun` holds, `[]` when none); `probe_of` (the `probeOf` string) exactly when `probeOf` was given, and otherwise no `probe_of` key at all, never `null` or `''`, because `certifyChecks` reads any `probe_of` key as a probe (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-bcfb66d3); and `environment`, the `RunResult.environment` array `run` returns, index-parallel to `results` (the shape gate.ts writes beside `results` on `testgate-result`), on clone, probe and scratch records alike, so every close-time and post-merge run has a per-check duration for the ledger (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-78c887e5). When `sleptDuringCheck(environment[i])` holds for a failed `results[i]`, the record also carries `error_class: 'execution.env-failure'` and `environment_evidence` (the failed checks' entries, as gate.ts names them), judged through task-1's exported `sleptFailedChecks` (testgate.ts), the one per-check rule gate.ts also uses; integration.ts holds no copy of it (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-6cc5bf43). The returned `IntegrationCheckRecord` keeps main's seven fields and gains optional `tiers?: CheckTier[]`, `tiersPresent?: CheckTier[]`, `treeSha?: string`, `notRun?: string[]`, `probeOf?: string`, `environment?: CheckEnvironment[]`, `errorClass?: 'execution.env-failure'` and `environmentEvidence?: CheckEnvironment[]`, which `runIntegrationCheck` sets to exactly what it wrote (task-7 reads them off the return value); `latestIntegrationCheck` and `latestIntegrationCheckAt` never set them. Export exactly `interface RunChecksAtOptions { setupCmd?: string; timeoutMs?: number; runAll?: boolean; environmentSources?: EnvironmentSources } interface RunChecksAtResult { setupFailed: boolean; setup: CheckResult | null; deps: DepsCheck | null; results: CheckResult[]; environment: CheckEnvironment[]; pass: boolean } function runChecksAt(projectDir: string, commit: string, checks: readonly CheckCommand[], opts?: RunChecksAtOptions): Promise<RunChecksAtResult>` (`EnvironmentSources`, `CheckEnvironment` and `CheckCommand` from testgate.ts, `DepsCheck` from gate.ts; `runAll` defaults to true, as the integration check runs today). `setup` is the setup command's result when `setupCmd` is given, else null; `deps` is gate.ts `checkWorktreeDeps`'s answer, or null when a failed setup stopped the run first; when `setupFailed` is true, `results` and `environment` are `[]` and `pass` is false. It creates a detached scratch worktree at `commit` under the same `.wt/<project>/` root queue.ts uses for batch candidates, named `scratch-<pid>-<uuid>` so no two runs collide; before adding it, removes (`git worktree remove --force`) every registered `scratch-<pid>-*` worktree under that root whose pid is not alive (heavyLock.ts `pidIsAlive`) and runs `git worktree prune`; runs `opts.setupCmd` first when given (its result returned as `setup`, never as a check), then gate.ts `checkWorktreeDeps`; a failed setup or a deps block returns `setupFailed` without running any check; otherwise runs the checks and returns their `results` with the run's `environment` beside them; removes the worktree in a `finally` whatever happens; never reads or changes the clone's branch, index or tree. Certification, defined here once and read by `remaining`, task-6 and task-7 (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3601e652, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-18712985, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-7f665588, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-fb7a5f11). Export exactly: `type CertificationReason = 'failed' | 'not-run' | 'changed' | 'no-result'; interface CertificationQuery { name: string; checkSha256: string } interface CheckCertification { certified: boolean; reason: CertificationReason | null; recordId: string | null; result: CheckResult | null } function certifyChecks(events: readonly StoredEvent[], epicId: string, commit: string, checks: readonly CertificationQuery[]): CheckCertification[]`. It is pure and returns one element per query, in the queries' order. Evidence for a query: an event whose `record.event_type` is `integration-check` and whose `payload.epic_id === epicId`; whose payload has no `probe_of` key (a `probe_of` of any value, string or not, makes the record a probe, and a probe never certifies); whose `payload.head_sha` is a string equal to `commit` (compared as strings: callers pass the full 40-hex sha, as `integrationHeadSha` returns it); and whose `payload.results` is an array. Inside such a record, an evidence element is a non-null object whose `name` is a string equal to the query's `name`. The matches are the evidence elements whose `check_sha256` is a string equal to the query's `checkSha256`. The deciding result is the last match: the one in the event with the highest index in the `events` array as given, and within that event the highest element index; never sorted by `ts`. With a deciding result: `certified` is true exactly when its `pass === true`, task-1's `isNotRun` is false for it, and its name is not in the record's `not_run` when `not_run` is an array; otherwise `reason` is `'not-run'` when `isNotRun` holds or the name is in `not_run`, else `'failed'`; `recordId` is that event's `event_id` and `result` is that element, certified or not. With no match: `certified` is false, `recordId` and `result` are null, and `reason` is `'changed'` when some evidence element carries a string `check_sha256` other than the query's, else `'no-result'`. `reason` is null exactly when `certified` is true. Nothing else is read: a field of the wrong type takes that record or element out of the evidence, so a malformed record can withhold certification and never grant it, and a record written before this epic (no `check_sha256` on its results) never certifies. So of a pass and a later fail for one digest at one commit the fail decides, a later record naming other checks never displaces an earlier record's result (certification is per check, not per record), and a tier move, which leaves `check_sha256` unchanged, never invalidates a result. Two readers beside it. `latestIntegrationCheckAt(events: readonly StoredEvent[], epicId: string, commit: string): IntegrationCheckRecord | null` returns the last `integration-check` event (`record.event_type === INTEGRATION_CHECK_EVENT`) whose `payload.epic_id === epicId`, in the given order, whose payload has no `probe_of` key and whose `head_sha` is a string equal to `commit`, projected exactly as `latestIntegrationCheck` projects a record (its seven fields), or null. `lastTieredRecordId(events: readonly StoredEvent[], epicId: string): string | null` returns the `event_id` of the last `integration-check` event whose `payload.epic_id === epicId`, in the given order, that uses tiers, or null (neither reader looks at any other event type; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-629614d7): an event uses tiers when its payload has a `probe_of` key, or has a `tiers` or `tiers_present` key whose value is anything other than a non-empty array every element of which is the string `'pre-merge'`. A record written before this epic (neither key) and a record of an unlabelled project (`['pre-merge']` in both) do not use tiers; a malformed `tiers` or `tiers_present` (a string, `[]`, an unknown tier) does, so it fails closed. There is no other fold: no `latestTierChecks`, no record classification and no per-tier view.
acceptance_criteria: test/integrationTiers.test.ts (write first; fails today because `tier` is ignored): at the clone root with tier `post-merge`, only post-merge checks run and the record carries `tiers: ['post-merge']`, `tiers_present`, a 40-hex `tree_sha`, and per result `cmd_sha256` and `check_sha256`; with `all` every check runs. `remaining`: with a passing post-merge record at the head, a file of pre-merge, post-merge and pre-release checks runs only the pre-merge and pre-release checks (fixture counter) and records `tiers: ['pre-merge', 'pre-release']`; after the post-merge check's command is edited, it runs that check too; after only its tier is moved, it does not; a check whose last result at the head is a pass followed by a fail for the same digest is selected again, because `remaining` selects through `certifyChecks` (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9f20e9f0). `certifyChecks` (test/integrationTiers.test.ts, written first; fails today because the export does not exist), against the exported types, each case asserting the whole returned `CheckCertification` (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-010cdcc0, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-8717758a, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b77f5fdb, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3601e652, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-a3bc5e33, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-f24b826c, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-18712985, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-f026d695, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-7f665588, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-fb7a5f11): a passing result at the commit under the queried digest is certified with that record's id and that element; a later passing post-merge-only record at the commit leaves a pre-release check's certification from an earlier `all` record unchanged; a pass then a fail for one digest at one commit give `reason: 'failed'` with the fail's record id, a fail then a pass give certified, and both orders hold when the two records' `ts` sort the other way (sorting by `ts` fails this test by name); a `heavy.wait-timeout` result and a passing result whose name is in its record's `not_run` give `'not-run'`; a result only under another `check_sha256` gives `'changed'`; a result with no `check_sha256` (a record written before this epic) and a result only at another commit give `'no-result'`; a passing probe at the commit gives `'no-result'` whether `probe_of` is a string or a number; another epic's record is ignored; no record gives `'no-result'`. Malformed evidence withholds and never grants: a record whose `results` is not an array, whose `head_sha` is a number, an element that is `null` or whose `name` is a number, and a result whose `pass` is the string `"true"` each leave the query uncertified (the last as `'failed'`). An empty query list returns `[]`. Mutation: making any one of these malformed shapes certify fails a named case.

Record shape (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-78c887e5): on a clone-root record, a probe record and a scratch record, `payload.environment` is an array beside `results` with one entry per result in the same order (`environment[i].name === results[i].name`), a measured entry has `window: 'command'` and a numeric `monotonic_ms`, the not-run heavy check of AC6 has `window: 'none'`, and no result carries an `environment` key. tasks.title: Epic close and verdict certify every declared check at the head
tasks.summary: Spec D5, AC5. With a checks declaration, `epic close` and `epic verdict` require each declared check certified at the integration head by task-5's `certifyChecks`, one blocker per uncovered check naming the check, its tier and one reason; an empty declaration and an unreadable head block. Without one, main's rule, strings and `summary.integration.check` stay byte for byte, except that an epic whose records use tiers is refused with one blocker asking for `--checks`.
tasks.objective: In factory/orchestrator/src/epic.ts the close and the verdict take an optional checks declaration and decide integration coverage by one of two rules, chosen only by whether the declaration was passed (spec D5). Types (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-010cdcc0, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-1937e8e2). Export exactly `interface DeclaredCheck { name: string; tier: CheckTier; checkSha256: string }` and `interface DeclaredCheckStatus extends DeclaredCheck { certification: CheckCertification | null }` (`CheckTier` from task-1's testgate.ts, `CheckCertification` from task-5's integration.ts). `EpicVerdictInput` gains `checks?: readonly DeclaredCheck[]`, which `EpicCloseInput` inherits: absent means no declaration, `[]` is an empty declaration, and task-14 sets it from `--checks`. `IntegrationStatus` keeps main's `check`, `headSha` and `branch` unchanged and gains `declared?: readonly DeclaredCheckStatus[]` and `tieredRecordId?: string`, both optional and left unset (never set to `undefined`) when they do not apply, so every builder of `{check, headSha, branch}` (test/epic.test.ts `okIntegration`, about line 191, and its `{check, headSha, branch}` literals such as the one about line 1653; test/specFindings.test.ts about line 1539; test/completedStaysCompleted.test.ts about line 166) (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-6825e4f4) compiles and passes unchanged and none is claimed. The reader. `computeEpicSummary` (about line 1750) builds the `IntegrationStatus` from the events it already reads, in their order, and reads no other event. Without `input.checks`: `check` is `latestIntegrationCheck(events, epicId)`, as on main; `declared` is unset; `tieredRecordId` is task-5's `lastTieredRecordId(events, epicId)` when that is non-null, else unset. With `input.checks`: `check` is task-5's `latestIntegrationCheckAt(events, epicId, head)`, or null when `input.integrationHeadSha` is null; `declared` is `input.checks` in its order, each element carrying `certification` from one `certifyChecks(events, epicId, head, input.checks)` call (index for index), or `certification: null` on every element when the head is null; `tieredRecordId` is unset. Blockers. `integrationBlockers` decides by the first match (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-8438cc28): (1) `declared` set and empty: one blocker, `Epic "<epic>" has an empty checks declaration, so no check can be shown certified at <branch>.`; (2) `declared` set and `headSha` null: one blocker, `Could not read the head of <branch>, so no declared check can be shown certified at it.`; (3) `declared` set: one blocker per element whose `certification.certified` is false, in declaration order, `Check "<name>" (<tier>) is not certified at <head8> of <branch>: <reason text>.`, and none when every element is certified; (4) `tieredRecordId` set: one blocker, `Epic "<epic>" has integration-check records written under check tiers (latest: <tieredRecordId>), so its close needs the checks declaration: pass --checks <file> to bs epic close and bs epic verdict.`; (5) otherwise main's body, unchanged and byte for byte: no record, unreadable head, stale, failed. `<head8>` is the head's first 8 characters, as main writes it. With a declaration the required set is the declaration and nothing else: it is never derived from the records, so no record can shadow, drop or add a required check, and a check with no record at all, only records written before this epic, only probes, or results only at older commits is `no-result` and blocks. Without a declaration, rule (4) replaces main's last-wins rule on any epic whose records use tiers, because the last record of a tiered epic is typically a post-merge batch run or a probe that ran part of the checks, and main's rule would certify the epic on it (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-d6c28b83; spec hard constraints 2 and 7); an unlabelled project's records never use tiers (task-5's `lastTieredRecordId`), so its close without a declaration is main's close. Reason text, from one exported function `certificationReasonText(c: CheckCertification): string | null`, null exactly when `c.certified` is true, used by the blockers and the judge prompt alike for uncertified checks only (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-4d1588f3): `failed` -> `its last result failed (exit <result.exitCode>, record <recordId>)`; `not-run` -> `its last result did not run (heavy.wait-timeout, record <recordId>)`; `changed` -> `its results there exist only under another check_sha256 (its name, command, heavy flag or timeout changed since they ran)`; `no-result` -> `no non-probe record there has a result for its check_sha256`.
