tasks.title: Post-merge batch: the branch, the trigger, the base, a red that ran and reproduces, and the bisect
tasks.summary: Spec D4, AC6. A library that pins the integration branch, decides whether a batch is due (dependency, batch, idle and final arms), finds a digest-aware base, runs the post-merge tier at the head in a prepared scratch worktree, refuses to blame never-run, env, flaky or pre-existing reds, and bisects a reproduced red over per-task merges to name a culprit.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/postMergeBisect.ts exporting `POST_MERGE_BATCH = 4` (commented with spec D4 as its source), `assertIntegrationBranch(projectDir, epicId)` (derives the branch only through worktree.ts `integrationBranchName(epic, epicBranchPrefix(project, epic))`, requires the `<prefix>/<epic>/integration` shape and refuses the default branch from `detectDefaultBranch`, with `postmerge.not-integration-branch`), `isBsRevertCommit(message)` (true when the message carries a `Bs-Revert-Of` trailer; task-16 validates all four), `postMergeBase(input)` (step 2 below as its own export: the base, whether it is observed, and the task merges since it with their `merge_sha`, the uncertified merges), `heldByPostMerge({tasks, edges, statusOf, uncertifiedMerges, hasPostMergeChecks})` (pure: every `todo` or `ready` plan task with a plan dependency on an uncertified merge, each with the merged task ids it waits on; empty whenever the effective checks hold no post-merge entry, so an unlabelled project never holds anything; OQ-v2-1 (c), operator answer bs-check-tiers-run-2026-10-30#40), `landedBsReverts(projectDir, epicId)` (spec D4's one scan: every first-parent commit from the integration branch's fork point from the default branch to the head whose message carries a `Bs-Revert-Of` trailer, oldest first, never bounded by the base) and `findPostMergeCulprit(input, ctx, opts)`. Input: epic id, project dir, the effective checks (each with its `checkSha256`, task-1's `checkDigest(entry)`), the plan's tasks and dependency edges, the epic's event lineage, `final`, `setupCmd`, and an injectable runner (default task-5's `runIntegrationCheck` with `workspace: 'scratch'`). Steps: (0) `assertIntegrationBranch`. (1) No post-merge entry -> `no-checks-in-tier`, nothing created: no worktree, no run and no record, so it certifies no check and nothing can read it as a passed tier; it says only that no batch is due (hard constraint 4, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3c48b247). (2) Base per spec D4: the latest ancestor of the head at which task-5's `certifyChecks` returns `certified: true` for every current post-merge check, each queried as a `CertificationQuery` `{name, checkSha256}` (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-a013bb67); else the fork point from the default branch, flagged unobserved. The head itself certified for all of them -> `no-new-merges`. This test comes before step (3), so `final` at a head already certified for every current post-merge check also returns `no-new-merges` and runs nothing: `final` is the arm that never returns `batch-not-ready`, not a forced re-run (spec D4; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-08764ccf). (3) Unless `final`, run only when a D4 arm holds: dependency (`heldByPostMerge` is non-empty, the same function `bs wave check` refuses by, so the trigger and the hold cannot disagree), batch (at least `POST_MERGE_BATCH` task merges since the base), idle (`inFlightTasks` names no epic task other than ones whose folded status is in `HELD_OPEN_BY_AN_OPERATOR`); else `batch-not-ready`, nothing created. Every check run this module makes is a scratch run through the runner, which has `runIntegrationCheck`'s signature and contract, with `workspace: 'scratch'`, that run's commit and the batch's `setupCmd`: the head run (4) and the probes of (7), (8) and (10), which also pass `probeOf` naming the head run's record. A failed setup or deps block in any of them is the thrown `IntegrationCheckError` with code `integration.setup-failed` (task-5: no record is written for that run); it ends the call at once with `setup-failed`, carrying `step` (`'head'`, `'reproduce'`, `'base'` or `'bisect'`), the `commit` whose setup failed, and every record and probe event id written before it (the red head record included), and with no culprit; the module moves no ref and writes no `wave-reverted` on it, as on every outcome. Any other thrown error propagates (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-ead87064, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-20bce6bf). (4) Run the post-merge tier at the head; setup failed -> `setup-failed` (`step: 'head'`); green -> `green`. (5) Any failed result for which `isNotRun` holds -> `lock-timeout`. (6) Every failed result env-classified -> `env-failure`. A failed `results[i]` of the head run's returned record is env-classified exactly when `sleptDuringCheck` holds for that record's `environment[i]` (task-5's array, index-parallel to `results`), the same per-check rule task-8 applies. The record-level `errorClass`, which task-5 sets when any one failed result slept, does not decide it, so a run in which only some failed results slept goes on to step (7) (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3307095e). (7) Re-run the failed checks at the head as a probe; any passes -> `not-reproduced`; a not-run result here -> `lock-timeout`. (8) An unobserved base is probed with the failed checks; red -> `red-at-base`. (9) First-parent commits base..head that are neither per-task merges (`Merge <task-id> into <branch>`) nor in `landedBsReverts` -> `batch-has-foreign-commit`. (10) Bisect the task merges, re-running only the failed checks at each prefix as probes (a not-run probe -> `lock-timeout`); culprit = the first merge whose prefix is red after an observed-green prefix. (11) A later merge in the batch with a plan dependency edge on the culprit -> `revert-has-dependents`, which also carries `dependents`, the task ids of those later merges in merge order; otherwise `culprit-found`. Both outcomes carry the same culprit, `culprit: {task, merge_sha, failing_checks, red_record_event_id}` (the culprit task id, its merge sha, the failing checks and the red head record's event id: the shape of task-12's `culprits` entries without `reproduced`), plus the merges in the batch and every record and probe event id (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-adee4fd6). This module never moves a ref and never writes `wave-reverted`; task-12 does. test/helpers/integrationRepo.ts exports its repo builder so task-12 and task-16 can import it without editing it: task merges, and a bs revert commit whose four trailers are parameters (`{revertOf, task, redRecord, failingChecks}`), each defaulting to the valid value the builder derives for the merge it reverts, each replaceable by any string and each omittable, so a caller can write a non-40-hex `Bs-Revert-Of`, an unknown `Bs-Task`, an unparseable `Bs-Red-Record` or an empty `Bs-Failing-Checks`.
acceptance_criteria: test/postMergeBisect.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist), on temp repos from test/helpers/integrationRepo.ts with three task merges where merge 2 breaks a post-merge check: outcome `culprit-found`, culprit task 2, and the probe records carry `probe_of` naming the head run.

Flaky head: the post-merge check fails once at the head and passes on the re-run (fixture alternates by a counter file) -> `not-reproduced` and no culprit. Under the null hypothesis (no re-run) the same fixture names merge 3; the test asserts no culprit, which differs.

Lock, through the objective's injectable runner, with no other seam (raised by the planner, no finding id): the runner returns the head run's heavy check not run (`reason: heavy.wait-timeout`, as `runHeavy` returns it) -> `lock-timeout`, no probe and no culprit. Returning it only for a bisect probe -> `lock-timeout`, no culprit.

Trigger: 2 merges with an epic task in flight and no dependent waiting -> `batch-not-ready` and no worktree created; the same with a `todo` task depending on merge 1 -> it runs; the same with the in-flight task `escalated` -> it runs (idle arm); `final` with a task in flight and no dependent waiting runs the tier and never returns `batch-not-ready`, while `final` at a head already certified for every post-merge check returns `no-new-merges` and runs nothing (the fixture's run counter is unchanged) (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-08764ccf).

Base: after a passing post-merge record at the head, editing a post-merge command (new `check_sha256`) makes the next call run instead of `no-new-merges`, and moving a check's tier does not; a new check that already fails at the fork point -> `red-at-base`, no culprit.

`landedBsReverts` finds a bs revert commit that is itself the latest certified commit (the base), and one older than the base; it ignores a hand-written commit with no `Bs-Revert-Of` trailer, and returns one whose other trailers are malformed (task-16 records it as `invalid-trailers`). Those commits come from the builder's trailer parameters: a default call writes four valid trailers, and a call overriding one trailer or omitting it writes exactly that change (asserted on the commit message).

Each other outcome has its own fixture: `no-checks-in-tier` (no record, no worktree), `setup-failed` (driven through the default runner, `runIntegrationCheck` with `workspace: 'scratch'` and a failing `setupCmd`, not only an injected one; `step: 'head'`, no record written), `env-failure` (the injectable runner returns the record task-5 writes for one failed result whose `environment` entry at the same index has `clock_gap_ms` at `SLEEP_GAP_MS`, with `errorClass` and `environmentEvidence` set as task-5 sets them; and, separately, two failed results of which only the first has that gap, with `errorClass` set as task-5 sets it for any slept failure, return no `env-failure` and go on to step (7)'s re-run, so a module that decides by `errorClass` fails this case by name; answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3307095e), `batch-has-foreign-commit` (a hand commit; a bs revert commit in the range is not foreign), `revert-has-dependents` (merge 3 depends on the culprit merge 2 by a plan edge: the result's `dependents` is `[task 3]` and it carries a `culprit` deep-equal to the one `culprit-found` returns on the same repo without that edge, with task 2, its merge sha, the failing checks and the red head record's id; answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-adee4fd6).

`assertIntegrationBranch` refuses when the derived branch would be the default branch (`main`) or lacks the `/integration` shape, before any worktree is created; with every fixture, the integration ref and the clone's branch, index and tree are byte-identical before and after.

Hold (test/postMergeBisect.test.ts, written first; fails today because `heldByPostMerge` does not exist): on the builder's repo with merges of A and B since the base, plan task C depending on A and plan task D depending on nothing, both `todo`, `heldByPostMerge` returns exactly C waiting on A; after a passing post-merge record at the head (task-5's writer) it returns nothing; with no post-merge entry in the checks it returns nothing; an admitted (`in-progress`) dependent is never listed. Probe-run setup failure (test/postMergeBisect.test.ts, written first; fails today because a probe's `integration.setup-failed` escapes as a raw `IntegrationCheckError`; answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-20bce6bf), through the default runner on the criterion-1 repo where merge 2 breaks a post-merge check and the base is observed (a passing post-merge record at the fork point is written first, so no base probe runs): a `setupCmd` that passes at the head and fails at commits that lack a file only merge 3 adds returns `setup-failed` with `step: 'bisect'`, the failing prefix's commit and the red head record's id among the event ids, no culprit, no ref moved and no `wave-reverted`; a `setupCmd` that fails on its second invocation (a counter file outside the worktree) returns `setup-failed` with `step: 'reproduce'` and the head's commit; with an unobserved base, a `setupCmd` that fails only at the fork point returns `setup-failed` with `step: 'base'`. tasks.title: The check ledger: identity, duration, class and unique catches per check per run
tasks.summary: Spec D6, AC8. A pure, read-only fold over gate, queue, integration and revert events that classifies each failure as real, flaky, env, not-run or unconfirmed, marks unique catches, severity and sensitive-path guards (failing closed on unknown tasks), and computes runs, minutes, flake rate, importance and merges per post-merge run.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/checkLedger.ts exporting `checkLedger(inputs, opts)`, a pure fold plus an injected tree-diff reader, and named constants `LEDGER_WINDOW_DAYS = 30` and `SEVERITY_WEIGHTS` (S1 8, S2 4, S3 2, S4 1), each commented with spec D6 as its source. `inputs` is task-13's `{events, taskIdOf, taskClaims, sensitiveGlobs}` (this module reads no file). Every task join goes through `taskIdOf` (event id -> qualified task id or `unattributed`). Run rows come from `testgate-result`, task-4's `queue-tier-run` records (one per queue tier run, `results` and `environment` side by side, `task_ids` naming the candidate; the landing and blocked events link a task to its run through `pre_landing_run_id`, and add no run of their own; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-aabfcf57), `integration-check` records (task-5's fields; probes are runs) and `wave-reverted`. Each row: identity (name plus `cmd_sha256`, or `name-only`), qualified task or epic, tiers, tree, outcome, duration from the `monotonic_ms` of the `CheckEnvironment` paired with the result by index: `payload.environment[i]` for `payload.results[i]` on `testgate-result`, on `integration-check` (task-5's field) and on `queue-tier-run` (task-4's event); a pair counts only when the entry's `name` equals the result's, and an absent array, a missing or mismatched entry, or `window: 'none'` gives `null`, never 0 (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-5d4a0377), class, unique or shadowed, severity, event id. Classes, unique catch, severity and the sensitive-path guard follow spec D6 exactly. The class vocabulary is five strings, exported as `FAILURE_CLASSES = ['not-run', 'env', 'flaky', 'real', 'unconfirmed']` and decided in that order: `unconfirmed` is a failure that ran and is none of not-run, env, flaky or real (no later pass of its identity at a different tree for the same task whose diff touches a path other than the checks file, and no confirmed revert of its culprit); it counts as a run with its minutes, and never as a catch or flaky evidence: it adds nothing to real catches, unique catches, importance or flake rate (spec D6; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3661495f). It protects the check as a real catch does, because a failure the ledger can confirm neither way is unverifiable, and D6 lets an unverifiable failure protect a check, never expose it (as an unreadable diff counts as real): per identity the ledger reports unconfirmed failures in the window, each with its event id and its D6 severity (S1 on a task that touches a sensitive path, fail closed as above, else S2: the rule a real catch uses), and the sensitive-path guard's catch arm counts an unconfirmed failure on such a task, however old, as it counts a real catch (spec D6, D7; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c9adc1ac). Further: a not-run result (task-1's `isNotRun`, or a name in a record's `not_run`) is counted only as `not_run`; a task that is `unattributed` or has no claims entry counts as touching a sensitive path; severity and the guard otherwise use security.ts `claimTouchesGlob` over the task's claims and `sensitiveGlobs`. The tree-diff reader defaults to `git diff --name-only --no-renames <a> <b>`; an unreadable diff makes the failure `real`. `name-only` rows count toward catches and guards, never runs or minutes. A `name-only` failure is classed like any other, and one classed `unconfirmed` protects exactly as a `name-only` real catch does: it counts, for every identity with that check name, in the unconfirmed failures in the window (so task-9's `itemBlocker` blocks the check) and in the sensitive-path guard's catch arm, and it adds no run or minute (spec D6: missing history can only protect a check; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-cb11d7ec). `opts.window` (`{from, to}`) applies to the numbers only; the sensitive-path guard's catch arm reads every event in `inputs`, however old (spec D6). Per identity over the window: runs, measured minutes, unmeasured and not-run counts, median minutes, flake rate, importance, real catches, S1/S2 catches in the window, unconfirmed failures in the window (each with its severity), guards-sensitive, and the event ids behind each number; and the D7 inputs R and M split by source (gate, queue, close). Project-wide: post-merge head runs (`--final` included), task merges, epics with merges, and merges per post-merge run. The env class is `sleptDuringCheck(entry)` (testgate.ts) on the paired entry of a failed result; no threshold is copied. test/helpers/ledgerEvents.ts builds every `testgate-result`, `integration-check` and `queue-tier-run` payload from a `RunResult` that a real `testgate.run` call returned with injected `environmentSources` (`results` and `environment` side by side, as gate.ts, integration.ts and queue.ts write them); no helper puts `environment` on a result.
acceptance_criteria: test/checkLedger.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist), fixtures from test/helpers/ledgerEvents.ts: env (gap at `SLEEP_GAP_MS`), flaky (same identity, same tree, a fail and a pass, as the D4 head re-run writes), real (fail at tree A, pass at tree B, diff touching `src/x.ts`), not-real (fail at A, pass at B, diff touching only the checks file) and not-run (`reason: heavy.wait-timeout`). Each gets a different class, `env`, `flaky`, `real`, `unconfirmed` and `not-run` respectively, and the test asserts each fixture's class string, so swapping any two definitions fails it. Separately, the exported `FAILURE_CLASSES` deep-equals, as a list in decision order, `['not-run', 'env', 'flaky', 'real', 'unconfirmed']` (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b297da1e). A fail at A never followed by a pass is `unconfirmed` too. An `unconfirmed` failure adds a run and its minutes and no real catch, unique catch or importance (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3661495f); it counts in the identity's unconfirmed failures in the window with severity S2, or S1 when its task claims `src/auth/session.ts`, and an S1 unconfirmed failure 40 days before `now` still marks the check guarding, as criterion 8's real catch does (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c9adc1ac).

Not-run: a check whose only failures are lock-wait timeouts has zero runs, zero minutes, zero catches and a `not_run` count equal to the timeouts; a bisect probe listing it in `not_run` adds nothing else.

Unique catch: C fails after faster F passed in the same run -> unique; C fails with faster F ordered after it (short-circuited) -> `shadowed`; F observed passing at the same tree in another record -> unique.

Severity and guard: a catch on a task claiming `src/auth/session.ts` is S1 and marks the check guarding; a check with 0 failures that ran on that task's gate inside the window is guarding too; outside the window with no catch it is not. A gate event whose `taskIdOf` entry is `unattributed`, or whose task has no claims entry, marks the check guarding (fail closed).

Identity: two rows with the same name and different `cmd_sha256` are two identities; a `name-only` real catch counts toward the guard but adds no run or minute; and a `name-only` unconfirmed failure (a record with no digest, never followed by a pass, on a task claiming `src/auth/session.ts`) appears in the unconfirmed failures in the window of the check of that name, marks that check guarding, and adds no run or minute (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-cb11d7ec).

A run with no `environment` array, with an entry whose `name` differs from its result's, or with `window: 'none'` has duration `null`; minutes sum measured runs only, with the unmeasured count beside them. An event in the shape no writer on the base produces (an `environment` object inside each result and no array beside `results`) yields duration `null` and no env class, so a fixture in that shape cannot pass the duration or env assertions. An unreadable tree diff (injected reader throws) yields `real` (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-5d4a0377).
Every number names its event ids; the fold writes nothing (inputs deep-equal before and after).

Window: a real catch on a task claiming `src/auth/session.ts` 40 days before `now`, with a 30-day window, still marks the check guarding (and task-9 then proposes nothing for it), while that catch adds nothing to the in-window runs, minutes, real catches or S1/S2 catches. A run on that task 40 days ago with no failure does not mark it guarding.

Measured from every source (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-5d4a0377, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-78c887e5 and f-bs-check-tiers/integration-aabfcf57): a `testgate-result`, a `queue-tier-run` and an `integration-check` record, each built by the helper from a real `run` result, all yield non-null durations equal to their entries' `monotonic_ms`; R and M split by source (gate, queue, close) each count at least one run; a red `queue-tier-run` whose failing check later passes at another tree for the same task counts as a queue catch; the `wave-merged` and blocked events whose `pre_landing_run_id` equals its `run_id` add no second run (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9a17ba19). Mutation: reading `results[i].environment` instead of the array fails this test by name.

Flaky is observed (same identity, same tree, both outcomes), never inferred from load or timing; a check that never ran is no evidence of anything.

tasks.title: Tier-move proposals: the formula, decisions.json, an apply that writes only the overlay, promotion
tasks.summary: Spec D7-D9, AC9, AC10. A read-only pending fold over undeclared entries with D7's minutes-saved formula per option, notices for declared entries, one validator shared by proposals and apply, an apply that writes the overlay and decision events only, a 90-day quiet decline, and automatic promotion of an overlay-demoted check.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/tierProposals.ts with module-level event-name constants `CHECK_TIER_DECIDED_EVENT`, `CHECK_TIER_PROMOTED_EVENT` and `CHECK_TIER_BATCH_ANSWERED_EVENT`, each written through an `event_type:` property in this file (apply's two appends; the `pending_event` `{event_type: CHECK_TIER_PROMOTED_EVENT, payload}` that promotion stores and then appends), so test/eventTypes.test.ts's scan sees all three written here; and named constants `MIN_RUNS = 20`, `MIN_MEASURED_MINUTES = 30`, `DECLINE_QUIET_DAYS = 90` (commented with spec D7 as their source). Export `pendingProposals(ledger, events, effectiveChecks, overlay, {epicId, writable, now})`, a pure fold that reads only its arguments (no `dir`, no git command, no file): `overlay` is task-15's `readOverlay` result, `writable` is task-15's `overlayWritable(dir)` result (`ok` or the reason) and `epicId` the epic whose lineage `answered_in_epic` reads, both computed by the caller (task-10's `bs checks proposals` from `--project` and `--epic`). It returns demote items exactly as spec D7 defines them (only entries with `tierSource` `default` or `overlay`), in the D7 proposal shape, with `options` computed by D7's formula from the ledger's R, M, d and project-wide B and E (`basis` names each input and whether it was measured or estimated; probes and not-run excluded; minutes rounded to 0.1); `notices` for declared entries (for example a declared post-merge check with a real catch); and task-15's overlay report. Stage-bound checks (gate.ts `stageBoundCheckNames`) are never proposed. Each item also carries task-8's `importance`; items are ordered by post-merge `minutes_saved`, largest first, then by `check`; and the result carries `answered_in_epic` (true when the lineage of `epicId` in `events` holds a `check-tier-batch-answered`). Export `validateDecisions(json, pending)` for the D7 decisions.json shape, and one `itemBlocker(item, ledger, effectiveChecks, now)` used by both `pendingProposals` (to exclude) and apply (to refuse). An unconfirmed failure (task-8's fifth class) protects as a real catch does: `itemBlocker` blocks an item whose check has any unconfirmed failure in the window, whatever its severity, just as D7's zero-real-catches rule blocks one with a real catch, under its own reason `an unconfirmed failure in the window` (it is not reported as an S1 or S2 catch, since it is no catch); and the sensitive-path guard `itemBlocker` reads already counts unconfirmed failures in its catch arm (task-8) (spec D6, D7; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c9adc1ac). `pendingProposals` returns no items, only a notice naming the reason, when `writable` is not `ok` or the ledger is `degraded` (spec D6, D8), so the batch never asks what apply would refuse. Export `applyTierDecisions(decisions, {dir, checksFile, effectiveChecks, actor, ledger, events, now}, ctx, opts)`: with task-15's `overlayPath(dir)` null it refuses `checks.overlay-not-a-repo` without locking or creating anything; a non-operator actor, or a decisions value that is not an array, is refused next with `items: []`, also before the lock, so nothing is created or repaired (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-55ecfc3c); otherwise, inside task-15's `withOverlayLock` (passing no `waitMs`, so task-15's default wait applies; a busy lock is the `checks.overlay-busy` refusal with `items: []`), first `reconcileOverlay`, then validate the whole array with `validateDecisions`, `itemBlocker` and `overlayWritable` against the repaired overlay, and refuse on any failure. Validation checks every item before it refuses. The refusal carries `items`, every failing item as `{proposal_id, check, reason}`, for an item's own causes: a shape error in the item, a check not in the file, a declared tier, a stage-bound check, a sensitive-path guard, an S1 or S2 catch in the window, an unconfirmed failure in the window. It carries `items: []` when the cause is the call's own: a non-operator actor, a decisions value that is not an array, an unwritable overlay, the lock held by a live writer (`checks.overlay-busy`), a failed repair. run.md step 12 reads `items` to re-run apply once without them (task-11; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b12b69b2). One rule for a refusal (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329): it appends none of this batch's events (no `check-tier-decided` and no `check-tier-batch-answered`) and writes none of this batch's decisions to the overlay. The only changes a refused call may leave are two. First, `reconcileOverlay`'s repair of what was already owed before the call (task-15's `overlayOwes`): the overlay entries of approved `check-tier-decided` and `check-tier-promoted` events already in the log, and the append, exactly as stored, of a `pending_event` the overlay already held. Second, the `.blacksmith/` directory the lock creates when it is absent (task-15; git tracks no empty directory, and no lock file stays). On a consistent overlay, where `overlayOwes` is empty, a refusal therefore leaves the log and the overlay byte-identical. A repair that itself fails (a task-15 `writeOverlay` refusal) refuses the whole call under that code, and the same rule holds. A call that takes the lock reconciles before it validates, so its batch is judged against the tiers the log already decided, and a crash converges on the next call that takes the lock, whatever that call's batch holds (spec D8). A call refused before it takes the lock (`checks.overlay-not-a-repo`, a non-operator actor, a decisions value that is not an array, or a lock still busy when the wait ends, `checks.overlay-busy`) runs no reconcile and repairs nothing; the repair waits for the next call that takes the lock (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-bd5b4ed3). Then, in this order (spec D8's crash order), append one `check-tier-decided` per item (payload: `proposal_id`, `check`, `cmd_sha256`, `from_tier`, `to_tier` or none, `decision`, `note`) and write the approved tiers to the overlay with `writeOverlay` and the revision read under the lock (decline writes no overlay entry). Every call that is not refused, an empty array included, finally appends one `check-tier-batch-answered` (`epic_id`, decided ids, pending ids) for the epic it is given, so a reply of `none` or an unparseable one is recorded and not asked again in that epic; a refused call appends none, so `answered_in_epic` stays false (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329). Export `recordBatchHandOff(epicId, {code, decisionsPath, pending}, ctx, opts): {eventId: string}` (the appended event's id) for the one case where the playbook hands a refused reply to the operator (task-11). It appends exactly one `check-tier-batch-answered` with `decided: []`, `pending` (the ids `pendingProposals` returns), and `handed_off: {code, decisions_path}`. It validates nothing of the reply, takes no lock and writes no overlay, so it decides nothing and every item stays pending. That event is the durable record that the batch was asked: the same fold that sets `answered_in_epic` reads it, so no later entry to step 12 asks again. The operator ends the hand-off by running an accepted `bs checks apply` with that decisions.json (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-852a2111). `pendingProposals` reads every `check-tier-batch-answered` of the epic's lineage alike for `answered_in_epic`. It also reports `handed_off`: the latest hand-off's `{code, decisions_path, event_id}` when no `check-tier-batch-answered` without `handed_off` follows it in that lineage, else null. The project's checks file is never opened for writing. Export `promoteAfterCatch(...)` for D7's automatic promotion: its evidence is a post-merge culprit result from task-7 (`{failing_checks, red_record_event_id, reproduced: true}`, spec D7), not the ledger. It returns one answer per entry of the culprit's `failing_checks`, in that order, each `{check, result, reason}`; every case below is an answer, never a throw (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-e4d115dc). Each check gets the answer of the first rule that applies. (a) The red record named by `red_record_event_id` is not in the events it is given (a resumed culprit whose record was lost), or holds no result with that check's name -> `result: 'promotion-skipped'`, `reason: 'red-record-unreadable'`. (b) The check declares its tier -> `declared-tier-wins`. (c) Its effective tier, from task-15's `resolveEffectiveTiers` over an unlocked `readOverlay(dir)`, does not have `tierSource: 'overlay'` from an approved `check-tier-decided` -> `not-promoted`, `reason: 'not-demoted'`; outside a git repository no check has an overlay tier, so every undeclared one ends here and the lock is never reached. (d) Its own failure in that record was not-run (task-1's `isNotRun`, or its name in the record's `not_run`) -> `not-promoted`, `reason: 'not-run'`; or env (`sleptDuringCheck` on the record's `environment` entry at that result's index, the per-check rule task-7 step (6) and task-8 use) -> `not-promoted`, `reason: 'env-failure'`. (e) Otherwise it promotes: inside `withOverlayLock` (passing no `waitMs`, so task-15's default wait applies), after `reconcileOverlay`, it writes the overlay entry as `pre-merge` with `pending_event` holding the `check-tier-promoted` payload (`check`, `cmd_sha256`, `from_tier`, `to_tier: pre-merge`, `catch_event_id`, `decided_by_event_id`), then appends that event and clears `pending_event` -> `promoted`. A busy lock or a refused write -> `promotion-skipped` with the code as `reason` (`checks.overlay-busy`, or a task-15 `writeOverlay` code such as `checks.overlay-tracked`), and the only change left is `reconcileOverlay`'s repair, by the same rule as a refused apply (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329). `reason` is null exactly for `promoted` and `declared-tier-wins`. Answers (a) to (d) are decided from the arguments and an unlocked `readOverlay` before the lock, so they take no lock, run no reconcile and change nothing on disk; only (e) takes the lock. task-14 prints these answers, and task-11 reports the `promotion-skipped` and `declared-tier-wins` ones. Vocabulary: this task is the first to write the three names, so it adds `check-tier-decided`, `check-tier-promoted` and `check-tier-batch-answered` to `gate_event` in factory/policies/taxonomy.yml with comments in the file's style, bumps `version` by one from the base's value, mirrors both in docs/specs/black-smith-architecture.md §8's yaml block, and updates the pinned version and history comment in test/taxonomy.test.ts, as task-2 did for `wave-reverted`; nothing else in those files changes. Version rule (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b21112c8): task-2, task-4 and task-9 each add names to taxonomy.yml and each bump `version` by exactly one from the value on that task's own base, in their claim-order edge order task-2 -> task-4 -> task-9, from main's 12. This task's base carries task-2 and task-4 (task-9 dependsOn task-2 and task-4, claim-order), which set 13 and then 14, so it moves `version` from 14 to 15: the same 15 in taxonomy.yml, in docs/specs/black-smith-architecture.md §8's yaml block (test/taxonomy.test.ts 'declares the same version' compares the two), and in test/taxonomy.test.ts's pinned `expect(tx.version).toBe(15)`, whose history comment gains one clause, `to 15 by bs-check-tiers task-9, which added ...` naming this task's names and dimension, after the clauses already there. If the base holds any other value, stop and report it in `notes` rather than choosing a number.
acceptance_criteria: test/tierProposals.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist): the D7 example (R 26, M 124.8, d 4.8, B 5 measured, E 1) gives options keep 0.0, post-merge 100.8, pre-release 120.0, each with `runs_covered` 26 and `minutes_spent` 124.8; with no post-merge runs and 20 merges, post-merge saves 28.8 and `basis` marks B estimated.

No proposal for 19 runs, a real catch in the window, an unconfirmed failure in the window (a red never followed by a pass, which protects as a real catch does; answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c9adc1ac), 29 minutes, a live decision, a sensitive-path guard, a check named `coverage`, or an entry that declares a tier; the declared post-merge check with a real catch appears under `notices`, not as an item.

`validateDecisions` accepts the D7 example and refuses each of: unknown key, unknown or decided `proposal_id`, `check` not matching the proposal, `approve` without `to_tier`, `to_tier` not among the item's options, `decline` with `to_tier`, a duplicate.

Every item `pendingProposals` returns passes `itemBlocker`, so applying an approve-all answer to an unchanged log never refuses. After a new S2 catch is appended between proposal and apply, `applyTierDecisions` refuses the whole array naming that item: no event appended, the overlay byte-identical. The same holds when the appended event is a red that the ledger classes `unconfirmed`, and the refusal names `an unconfirmed failure in the window` (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c9adc1ac). Crash, then refuse (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329), written first: (1) The fixture builds the crash state directly, with no injected throw: the log holds an approved `check-tier-decided` whose tier the overlay lacks, which is what a crash between apply's events and its overlay write leaves. A batch with one invalid item follows. That batch is refused naming the item. The overlay then holds exactly the approved tiers of the earlier, logged decisions (reconcile's repair) and none of this batch's. The log gains no event: no `check-tier-decided` and no `check-tier-batch-answered`, and `pendingProposals` then reports `answered_in_epic: false`. (2) When the overlay instead holds a stored `pending_event` (a promotion's crash state, written directly with task-15's `writeOverlay`), the refused call's only appended event is that owed `check-tier-promoted`, exactly as stored. (3) On a consistent overlay a refused call leaves the log's line count and the overlay's bytes unchanged. (4) A batch whose two items both fail (one gained a real catch, one an unconfirmed failure) is refused with both in `items`, each with its reason; the same batch without those two items is then accepted and appends its `check-tier-batch-answered`; a non-operator actor's refusal carries `items: []` (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b12b69b2); on the crash state of (1), that refusal and a `{}` refusal, both made before the lock is taken, each leave the overlay's bytes and the log's line count unchanged, because only a call that takes the lock reconciles (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-bd5b4ed3). (5) Mutation: skipping reconcile on the refusal path fails the repair assertion by name. Writing this batch's decisions or its `check-tier-batch-answered` before validation fails the 'none of this batch's' assertion.

A valid batch appends one `check-tier-decided` per item and then writes the approved tiers to the overlay; the checks file's bytes and mtime are unchanged, including when the file is tracked by git. Callers rely on the default wait (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-d8298da8): the test holds the lock through task-15's `withOverlayLock` in this process, never by writing `check-tiers.lock` itself, with an `fn` that waits on a promise the test resolves after 1 s (real timers) (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-97b65272). Called with no `waitMs` while it is held, a valid `applyTierDecisions` and a writing `promoteAfterCatch` both wait, and then succeed once it is released. A caller that passed `waitMs: 0` would fail this by name.

Crash convergence, from the two states a crash between the two writes leaves, each built directly, with no injected throw and no seam (raised by the planner, no finding id): (1) Events written, overlay not: the log holds approved `check-tier-decided` events whose tiers the overlay lacks, and `resolveEffectiveTiers` still gives those checks their earlier tier. The next `applyTierDecisions` call (an empty batch) reconciles: the overlay then holds the approved tiers, no `check-tier-decided` is duplicated, and the call appends only its own `check-tier-batch-answered`. (2) Overlay written, event not: the overlay holds the check's entry at `pre-merge` with a stored `pending_event`, and the log holds no `check-tier-promoted`. The next `applyTierDecisions` call (an empty batch) appends exactly one `check-tier-promoted`, exactly as stored, and clears `pending_event`; a further call appends no second one. `pendingProposals` is a pure fold and writes nothing; task-10 tests the same convergence through `bs checks proposals`, which runs `reconcileOverlay` before it.

`pendingProposals` called with `writable` `unreadable` (a corrupt overlay), `tracked` (its location tracked by git) or `not-a-repo`, each as task-15's `overlayWritable(dir)` returns it for that fixture, returns no items and a notice naming that reason; the fold is given no `dir` and runs no git command. For the same three locations `applyTierDecisions` refuses before appending anything.
A decided item does not resurface; a declined one is absent at day 89 and present at day 91.

`promoteAfterCatch` with a culprit result naming an overlay-demoted check returns `[{check, result: 'promoted', reason: null}]`, sets the overlay entry to `pre-merge` and appends `check-tier-promoted`, for each of the outcomes `reverted`, `revert-has-dependents` and `revert-red` (the evidence is the same). Each other answer is asserted whole (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-e4d115dc): a declared post-merge check gives `declared-tier-wins` with `reason: null`; an overlay-demoted check whose own failure was env-classified gives `not-promoted` with `env-failure`, and one whose failure was not-run gives `not-promoted` with `not-run`; an undeclared check with no overlay entry gives `not-promoted` with `not-demoted`; with the red record absent from the events, each failing check gives `promotion-skipped` with `red-record-unreadable`. A culprit with two failing checks, one overlay-demoted and one declared, gets two answers in `failing_checks` order, `promoted` then `declared-tier-wins`. The no-promotion answers take no lock and run no reconcile, pinned by two separate fixtures (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-a94b362c). (i) Held lock, on an overlay that owes a repair: the test holds the lock through `withOverlayLock` in this process, never by writing `check-tiers.lock` itself, its `fn` waiting on a promise the test settles after the assertions (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-97b65272). With vitest fake timers advanced past `OVERLAY_LOCK_WAIT_MS`, each of the five no-promotion answers above still resolves as stated (an answer that waited on the lock would come back as `promotion-skipped` with `checks.overlay-busy` instead), and the lock file's bytes and the overlay's bytes are unchanged. The busy answer itself, in the same fixture (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-560c24da): an overlay-demoted check whose own failure ran and did not sleep, one rule (e) would promote, resolves to `[{check, result: 'promotion-skipped', reason: 'checks.overlay-busy'}]` once the timers pass `OVERLAY_LOCK_WAIT_MS`, and never rejects. No `check-tier-promoted` is appended, no reconcile runs, and the lock file's bytes and the overlay's bytes are unchanged. Mutation: letting task-15's `checks.overlay-busy` escape `promoteAfterCatch` as a throw fails this by name. (ii) No `.blacksmith/` and no lock held: in a repo with no `.blacksmith/`, the three answers reachable without an overlay (`declared-tier-wins`, `not-promoted` with `not-demoted`, and `promotion-skipped` with `red-record-unreadable`) each resolve as stated, and no `.blacksmith/` is created.

Ordering and importance: three eligible items with post-merge savings 10, 40 and 25 come back in the order 40, 25, 10, each with `importance` 0; a check with a unique catch shows its non-zero importance in the ledger and is not proposed.

Batch answered: `applyTierDecisions([])` for epic E appends exactly one `check-tier-batch-answered` and nothing else; `pendingProposals` with `epicId` E then reports `answered_in_epic: true`, and with another `epicId` `false`, over the same events. Hand-off (written first; answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-852a2111): (1) After `applyTierDecisions` is refused with `items: []` on a decisions value that is not an array (`{}`), which task-9 refuses with `items: []` before it takes the lock (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-1c08e1c9, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-55ecfc3c), `recordBatchHandOff` for epic E with that refusal's code appends exactly one `check-tier-batch-answered`, with `decided: []` and `handed_off` naming that code and the decisions.json path. (2) It takes no lock: with the lock held for the whole call through `withOverlayLock` in this process, never by writing `check-tiers.lock` itself (as in criterion 9's held-lock fixture), and vitest fake timers advanced past `OVERLAY_LOCK_WAIT_MS`, it still resolves and appends its event, and it leaves the overlay's bytes and the lock file's bytes unchanged (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c1cd0860, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-97b65272). (3) `pendingProposals` with `epicId` E then reports `answered_in_epic: true`, the same items still pending, and that `handed_off`. (4) After a later accepted `applyTierDecisions` of a valid decisions.json approving one item, `handed_off` is null and that item is gone. (5) Mutation: making `answered_in_epic` count only events without `handed_off` fails this by name.

Vocabulary: the three `check-tier-*` names are in taxonomy.yml `gate_event` and architecture §8, the version is one higher than the base's, 15 on task-4's 14, in taxonomy.yml, §8 and test/taxonomy.test.ts (pinned `toBe(15)`, with a history clause `to 15 by bs-check-tiers task-9` after task-2's and task-4's) (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b21112c8), and test/eventTypes.test.ts and test/taxonomy.test.ts pass. tasks.title: The `bs checks` namespace (ledger, proposals, apply) and the overlay in readChecksFile
tasks.summary: Spec AC1, AC8-AC10, AC12, D8. `readChecksFile` resolves the overlay so every verb sees effective tiers; ships `bs checks ledger|proposals|apply` with the namespace-wide flags (proposals and apply also take the event envelope, because both can append); removes the scope doc's PLANNED-NAMESPACE marker in the same commit.
tasks.objective: In cli.ts, make `readChecksFile(filePath, {dir})` resolve effective tiers with task-15's `resolveEffectiveTiers` against the overlay of `dir`'s project root (`dir` is optional and names the directory whose overlay applies: `--worktree` for `bs gate run`, and for `bs results check --as gate`, which stands for that gate line and already takes `--worktree`; for `bs brief compose --checks`, its `--worktree` when given, and when it is not given no overlay is read, so undeclared entries stay `pre-merge`, the earliest tier, the brief lists no fewer checks than a gate would run, and the verb prints one line saying the overlay was not applied; `--project` for `bs queue run`, `bs integration check`, `bs epic close`, `bs epic verdict` and the `checks` verbs; with no `dir`, declared tiers only, as before this task; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-fd5faa29), setting `tier` and `tierSource` on each entry; an unreadable overlay resolves every undeclared entry to `pre-merge` and the verb prints that it did. Add the `checks` namespace in cli.ts and usage.ts with flags that mean what they mean on every existing verb: `--project <dir>`, `--specs-dir <dir>` (the parent of `<epic>/plan*.json`), `--state-dir <dir>`, `--now <iso>`. `bs checks ledger --project <dir> --specs-dir <dir> [--checks <file>] [--state-dir <dir>] [--now <iso>]` gathers inputs with task-13's `gatherLedgerInputs` and prints task-8's `checkLedger` as JSON, plus task-13's warnings and `degraded` flag, and, with `--checks`, task-15's overlay report. `bs checks proposals` takes the same flags plus a required `--checks <file>` and `--epic <id>` and the required envelope flags `--session <id> --plan-version <n> --causal-parent <event-id>`, which mean what they mean on `bs checks apply` and `bs checks post-merge`; a missing one exits 1 naming it before anything is read or written. When task-15's `overlayPath(dir)` is null (outside a git repository) it takes no lock, runs no reconcile, creates nothing, and prints `pendingProposals` with `writable: 'not-a-repo'` (no items, the notice), exit 0. Otherwise it reads the overlay and the events without the lock and asks task-15's `overlayOwes`; when nothing is owed (always so in a project with no `.blacksmith/` directory, where nothing was ever applied) it takes no lock and creates no directory or file. Only when something is owed does it run task-15's `reconcileOverlay` under `withOverlayLock`, passing no `waitMs`, so task-15's default wait applies (a busy lock is task-15's `checks.overlay-busy`, which writes nothing), with `ctx` built from those three flags, so an owed `check-tier-promoted` is appended in the playbook's own session, at its plan version, chained to the given causal parent (its only possible writes are entries and events an earlier apply or promotion already owed), then prints task-9's `pendingProposals` (items, notices, overlay report, `answered_in_epic`), calling it with `epicId` from `--epic` and `writable` from task-15's `overlayWritable(dir)`, which this verb computes so the fold stays pure. `bs checks apply <decisions.json> --checks <file> --project <dir> --specs-dir <dir> --epic <id> --actor <actor> [--state-dir <dir>] [--now <iso>] --session <id> --plan-version <n> --causal-parent <event-id>` calls `applyTierDecisions` and exits 1 on any refusal, printing one JSON document with the refusal's code, its message and task-9's `items` (every failing item with its reason; empty when the cause is not an item), which run.md step 12 reads (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b12b69b2). With `--hand-off <refusal-code>` it calls task-9's `recordBatchHandOff` instead, with that code, the decisions.json path and the ids task-9's `pendingProposals` returns. It validates nothing of the file, takes no lock, writes no overlay, appends that one event under the envelope flags, prints `{"event_id": <that id>}` and exits 0; `--hand-off` with no value exits 1 naming the flag (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-852a2111). The CLI parses flags and calls the library functions only. Remove `<!-- PLANNED-NAMESPACE: checks -->` from docs/specs/check-tiers-scope.md in the same commit and turn its `bs checks post-merge` code spans into prose that says the verb ships with task-14, so the doc guards hold on this tree. In that commit change test/checkTiersScopeDoc.test.ts's assertion that the doc carries the `PLANNED-NAMESPACE: checks` marker on its own line into an assertion that it carries no such marker: task-3 wrote that test, task-10 claims it for this one edit, a replacement of equal strength rather than a loosening, and every other assertion in the file stays as task-3 wrote it (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-a24cf08b).
acceptance_criteria: test/checksCli.test.ts (write first; fails today because `checks` is not a namespace): `bs checks ledger` on a fixture state dir with two projects' epics under two specs dirs prints only the epics under `--specs-dir`; a specs dir whose plans name two projects exits 1 with `checks.mixed-projects`; `bs checks proposals` prints the D7 example's three options.

Overlay resolution: with an overlay entry moving undeclared check `e2e` to post-merge, `bs gate run` from a task worktree of the same repo defers `e2e` with `tier_source: 'overlay'`; with `e2e` declaring `tier: pre-merge` in the file, the gate runs it (the declaration wins) and `bs checks proposals` reports the overlay entry `shadowed`.

tasks.summary: Spec AC3, AC5, AC7, AC9, AC11, AC12. wave.md step 10 passes the checks file to the queue; run.md's rolling admission runs the post-merge batch in the background before `bs wave next`; a reverted task reopens with the revert's log in the brief; close runs `--final` then `--tier remaining`; the proposal batch is one question; operator guides and CHANGELOG follow.
tasks.objective: Edit .claude/skills/bs/wave.md: step 7 gates the pre-merge tier and keeps the rule that the unit check is the project's full test command, in whatever tier the full suite sits. Step 10 adds `--checks <file>` beside today's `--test-cmd` (and `--select-test-cmd` where used) and says the queue keeps today's command for an unlabelled file and runs neither command, without refusing either flag, once a later tier exists (spec D2); step 10 also says that the post-merge batch is the epic session's, never the runner's, because the runner never admits. Step 8 gains one sentence beside its pinned compose sentence: with a tiered checks file the composed brief lists only the pre-merge checks the gate runs and names the deferred ones (task-1). In .claude/skills/bs/run.md's rolling-admission section add the post-merge rule as a block of its own, with the bold lead-in `**Post-merge and held tasks.**`, after the dispatched-runner bullet (spec D4; OQ-v2-1 (c), operator answer bs-check-tiers-run-2026-10-30#40; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-673a9c3e, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-8a0a6d8d). On each landing the epic session sees (inline: a `bs queue run` it ran returned `merged`; dispatched: a `wave-merged` on the tail it watches), it (1) starts `bs checks post-merge` with `--project`, `--checks`, `--plan`, `--setup-cmd` (the install command the playbook runs in task worktrees) and the envelope flags, and with no `--specs-dir`, which the verb does not take (task-14; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-fd7db283), `--session` being the epic session's own id, so its record lands in the log the hold reads as a background task (`run_in_background`, the command ending `; echo EXIT=$?`), waited on by its completion notification or the Monitor tool, never wrapped in `bs heavy run` (its checks take the heavy lock themselves; a lock wait can outlast a foreground call's 10-minute cap) (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-79215b80); (2) runs `bs checks post-merge --held --session <id>` with that same session id (read-only; it returns at once) and `bs wave next`; (3) admits at once every task `bs wave next` returns that `--held` does not list; (4) when the batch returns a proceed outcome, meaning one of the five outcomes the verb exits 0 on (`green`, `reverted`, `no-checks-in-tier`, `no-new-merges`, `batch-not-ready`; task-14), runs `bs checks post-merge --held --session <id>` and `bs wave next` again and admits every task `bs wave next` returns that `--held` no longer lists (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-2010bf19). No outcome releases a held task by itself: the re-read of `--held` recomputes the hold from records, so after `no-new-merges` it admits what an earlier call's record already certified, and after any outcome it admits only what the records no longer hold (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-cd1e92f1). The block writes steps (1) to (4) as four column-0 bullet items that open with the bold labels `**(a)**`, `**(b)**`, `**(c)**` and `**(d)**` (`- **(a)** ...`), one per step, each label used nowhere else in run.md, because steps (b) and (d) both run `--held` and `bs wave next` and the offset test anchors each step by its label (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-fc2ac27c). Never a numbered list: test/waveTier.test.ts scans run.md with `/^(\d+)\. /gm` and requires that no step number from 2 to 10 appears in it, so a column-0 `2.` to `4.` fails it, and an indented numbered list would render nested under the step before it (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-160116d6). The other line-shape scrapers of the files this task edits bind the same way: no new line in run.md, wave.md or queue-and-gate.md starts with `<digits>. ` at any indentation (waveTier, handbackPreflight's wave.md step and branch markers and queue-and-gate.md section 5's branch markers, playbookSlice, cliOptimize, integrationPrFactPack's and playbookOptimize's step-17 and step-18 bounds read those shapes); the block adds no heading; and it names neither `TaskStop` (playbookOptimize takes run.md's first paragraph holding both `TaskStop` and `EXIT=` as the TaskStop rule, and step (a)'s command ends in `EXIT=`) nor a double-quoted name followed directly by `above` or `below` (playbookCitations reads that as a section citation). The block says in words that 'right away' and 'at once' in the sentences above apply to every task `--held` does not list, and that `bs wave check` itself refuses a held task (`wave.held-by-post-merge`) and, on an epic whose records use tiers (task-5's `lastTieredRecordId` is non-null: a post-merge, a pre-release-only or a probe record alike, the predicate task-14 refuses by and task-6 refuses a close by; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-5bad56cc), a `wave check` line without `--checks` (`wave.checks-required`); so the pinned sentences stay word for word and the playbook gives one instruction per landing. Every `bs wave check` line in run.md and wave.md carries `--session <id>`, `--checks <file>` and `--project <dir>`, because the hold is read from that session's lineage and a session-less check reads no log (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-dc4b6bce). The rule handles each outcome: `green`, `no-checks-in-tier`, `no-new-merges`, `batch-not-ready` move on, and the block says that only `green` means the post-merge tier ran and passed, while the other three mean no batch was due and nothing ran, so the playbook never reports them as a passed tier (hard constraint 4, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3c48b247); `reverted` logs and lets rolling admission re-admit the task; `env-failure`, `not-reproduced` and `lock-timeout` are logged (`execution.env-failure`, `execution.flaky-test`, `execution.env-failure`) and the verb is called once more, a second at the same head goes to the operator (spec OQ6); `revert-recorded` (a revert that stands without a bounce) and every other outcome go to the operator with the JSON. `promotion-skipped` and `declared-tier-wins` are not outcomes but `result` values of entries in the `promotions` list task-14 prints beside one (task-14 states the entry shape), so the outcome's own rule applies and the playbook also reports each entry with either value to the operator once (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-4d400167, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-e4d115dc); for `revert-not-applicable` with reason `not-in-live-plan` the playbook names the three ways out spec D4 gives (an amendment that re-adds the task, an amendment adding a task that fixes the defect, an edit to the failing check) and offers no waiver, because no verb waives a red tier. In wave.md, step 9 reopens a reverted task with `bs worktree create <project> <epic> <task> --reopen --revert <revert-sha>`, puts the latest `wave-reverted`'s `failing_checks`, `log_tail` and `red_record_event_id` into the coder's brief, and counts the round on the S2 ladder. When the reopen refuses (`worktree.reopen-dirty`, `worktree.reopen-not-ancestor`, `worktree.reopen-revert-not-on-integration` or `worktree.reopen-revert-conflict`, task-14; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-8a4bca7f), step 9 says so in one sentence, not a new bullet. It hands the refusal to the operator once, does not admit the task again until the operator answers, and names the way out task-14 gives: a plan amendment that supersedes the task with one cut from the integration head (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-59c68d05). Edit .claude/skills/bs/run.md in this order (spec D5): first the playbook runs `bs checks proposals --epic <id>` with the envelope flags `--session`, `--plan-version` and `--causal-parent`, as for `bs checks apply`. If that call exits 1 (for example `checks.overlay-busy`), the playbook reports its error JSON to the operator once and goes on to `bs checks post-merge --final` without asking: bs never asks what it cannot apply, and nothing has moved (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-4164a46b). Only when it has items and `answered_in_epic` is false (step 12's first pass) does it ask ONE question for the whole batch, numbering items 1..n and lettering each item's options (a = keep) with their runs covered, minutes spent and minutes saved, and stating D7's reply grammar (`<n><letter>` tokens, or `none`); it turns the reply into the D7 decisions.json (a parse failure, an unknown item or letter, or a repeated item decides nothing), and runs `bs checks apply --epic <id>` until one call is accepted, at most twice, with `[]` when nothing was decided. Step 12 writes the three apply lines as three column-0 bullet items that open with the bold labels `**Apply.**` (the first call), `**Re-run.**` (the second call, without the refused items) and `**Hand-off.**` (the `--hand-off` call). Each label is used nowhere else in run.md, because step 12 now holds three `bs checks apply` lines and its tests anchor on the labels (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9ab7c010). Every labelled item, here and in the post-merge block, runs from its label to the first blank line or column-0 line after it. Its tests read the item's whole text with line breaks joined to spaces, so hard wrapping never moves an anchor (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-36e2f6e5). Every reply then ends in exactly one accepted apply, or in the operator's hands (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b12b69b2): (1) If the first call is refused with `items` (each item whose guardrail or shape now fails, which only a change to the log between question and answer causes), the playbook reports each item and its reason to the operator. It then runs apply once more with the same decisions minus those items (`[]` if none remain), because guardrails win over a reply and the batch is never asked twice. (2) A refusal with `items: []` (the actor, the overlay, the lock, a failed repair), or a second refusal, goes to the operator with the JSON and the decisions.json path. The playbook then runs `bs checks apply <decisions.json> --hand-off <refusal-code>` with the envelope flags (task-10). That call records the hand-off as the epic's `check-tier-batch-answered`, decides nothing, and turns `answered_in_epic` true, so no later entry to step 12 asks again. The hand-off ends when the operator runs `bs checks apply` with that decisions.json once the cause is fixed, or when the operator leaves the tiers as they are, which moves nothing (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-852a2111). Notices are reported, not asked; silence changes nothing. Then step 12 runs `bs checks post-merge --final` and then `bs integration check --tier remaining` at the clone root; when that call refuses with `integration.nothing-remaining`, every check is already certified at the head, so step 12 goes on to `bs epic verdict` and `bs epic close` exactly as after a green run, and any other refusal stops the close (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-059cacdc). Then verdict and close, both passing `--checks`. Update .claude/agents/bs-wave-runner.md only where it restates these steps. In docs/guide/operator-guide/queue-and-gate.md §5 document `tier` beside `heavy` and `timeout_ms`, the default, the empty-file rule, the overlay (location, declared-wins, shadowed and orphaned entries), and link docs/specs/check-tiers-scope.md; in closing-an-epic.md §7a document per-tier close and `--tier remaining`, and that `bs epic close` without `--checks` on an epic whose records use tiers is refused with one blocker that asks for `--checks`. Update the scope doc's status lines to shipped, and in the same commit change test/checkTiersScopeDoc.test.ts's assertion that each part's heading is followed by `Status: planned.` to assert `Status: shipped.`: task-3 wrote that test, task-11 claims it for this one edit, a replacement of equal strength rather than a loosening, and every other assertion in it stays as task-3 and task-10 left it (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-a24cf08b). Write the CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry from the other tasks' notes, task-18's scaffolded CI included. Every sentence the tests named in criterion 5 pin stays word for word; the new rules are new sentences beside them (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-92be2499).

tasks.summary: Spec D1, D4, AC6. Orchestrates a post-merge batch: runs task-16's resume first, calls task-7's bisect, preflights the bounce, builds the culprit revert with `git revert -m 1` (git 2.38), tests it with the pre-merge and post-merge tiers and records those runs at the revert commit, lands it through queue.ts landCandidate on the pinned integration branch, then writes wave-reverted.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/postMerge.ts exporting `runPostMerge(input, ctx, opts)`. `input` carries task-7's `findPostMergeCulprit` input as task-7 lists it, its injectable runner included (default task-5's `runIntegrationCheck` with `workspace: 'scratch'`), and passes it to task-7 unchanged. Every check run `runPostMerge` makes goes through that one runner: task-7's head run and probes, and R's two runs in step (4). So a test reaches R's runs through the runner task-7 already declares, and this task adds no seam for them (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-cb1c0515). Its `opts` may carry `onScratch?: (scratchPath: string) => void`, a test seam called once with step (3)'s scratch worktree path right after it is created; the CLI never passes it (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-65a5c329). `liveTaskIds` are the ids of the input plan's records whose `task_status` is not `superseded` (the plan `bs checks post-merge --plan` read, the file `bs wave next` reads). (0) Call task-7's `assertIntegrationBranch`, then task-16's `resumeLandedReverts` with `liveTaskIds`; when it wrote anything, return its outcome and `resumed: true`. The result shape is `{outcome, resumed, reason?, setup_failed?, dependents?, culprits, revert_sha?, event_ids}`, where `setup_failed` is `{step: 'head' | 'reproduce' | 'base' | 'bisect' | 'revert', commit: string}` and is set exactly when `outcome` is `setup-failed`: task-7's `step` and `commit` for a setup failure inside `findPostMergeCulprit`, and `{step: 'revert', commit: R}` for one while R is tested (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-4de860d8). `dependents` is task-7's `dependents` (the task ids of the later merges that depend on the culprit) and is set exactly when `outcome` is `revert-has-dependents` (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9c5f3805). `culprits` is a list of `{task, merge_sha, failing_checks, red_record_event_id, reproduced: true}`: on every outcome reached after task-7 named a culprit (task-7's `culprit-found`, and its `revert-has-dependents`, which carries the same `culprit`; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-adee4fd6) it holds that one culprit, task-7's `culprit` with `reproduced: true`; on a resumed return (step 0) it holds the `culprit` of each resumed write that has one (task-16, rebuilt from the trailers); otherwise it is empty. task-14 promotes on every entry (spec D7), so a check whose catch was recorded by a resume after a crash is promoted like any other. (1) Call task-7's `findPostMergeCulprit`; on `revert-has-dependents` return that outcome with `culprits` holding its culprit and `dependents` copied from task-7, and build nothing; return any other outcome but `culprit-found` unchanged, carrying its `step` and `commit` as `setup_failed` when the outcome is `setup-failed`. (2) Preflight: `waveRevertBlocker` for the culprit with `liveTaskIds`; a reason -> `revert-not-applicable` with that `reason` on the result, nothing built. For `not-in-live-plan` (a plan amendment dropped the finished culprit before this batch ran) nothing is reverted: the culprit's change stays on the integration branch, the head stays uncertified so close keeps refusing, and the outcome goes to the operator once with the culprit, the failing checks and the red record. The answer is one of three things, each of which re-certifies the head: a plan amendment that re-adds the task (plan.ts `draftNextVersion` accepts an added id the previous version does not hold live, so the next batch reverts and bounces it), a plan amendment adding a task that fixes the defect, or an edit to the failing check. No verb waives a red tier, so none is offered (spec D4). (3) Build: in a scratch worktree detached at the head (same `.wt/<project>/` root, named `scratch-<pid>-<uuid>`, task-5's scheme, so task-5's dead-pid sweep removes one a killed process left (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-71580e69), removed in a `finally`), `git revert -m 1 --no-edit <culprit-merge>` then amend the message to carry the four trailers (`Bs-Revert-Of`, `Bs-Task`, `Bs-Red-Record`, `Bs-Failing-Checks`); a conflict is aborted (`git revert --abort`) -> `revert-conflict`. (4) Test the revert commit R with the pre-merge tier and then the whole post-merge tier through that runner with `workspace: 'scratch'`, `commit: R`, the batch's `setupCmd` and the current digest, writing both as certifying records at R (each record's `head_sha` is R, task-5); a not-run result -> `lock-timeout`; a thrown `integration.setup-failed` (task-5: no record is written) -> `setup-failed` with `setup_failed: {step: 'revert', commit: R}`; any other red -> `revert-red` (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-ead87064). (5) Land R with queue.ts `landCandidate(projectDir, integrationBranch, head, R, message)`, where `integrationBranch` comes only from the branch `assertIntegrationBranch` returned; `landCandidate` is exported from queue.ts by this task without other change; `integration-dirty` and `integration-moved` are returned and nothing is written after step (4)'s two records at R. (6) After `landed`, `recordWaveReverted` (`disposition: bounce`) with the failing checks, the log tail, the red record id and every record and probe id -> `reverted`. A revert that breaks a pre-merge check only (the culprit's export is imported by a later file; a pre-merge typecheck-like check fails after the revert) -> `revert-red`, ref unchanged. A revert conflict -> `revert-conflict`, ref unchanged, no revert in progress left in any worktree. Two fixtures reach R's runs through the input's runner, task-7's injectable runner, with no other seam (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-cb1c0515). Pinned branch: with the epic's prefix configured so the derived branch would be the default branch, `runPostMerge` throws `postmerge.not-integration-branch` before any worktree is created, and `main` is unchanged.

The mechanism runs on git 2.38: the module uses no `merge-tree --merge-base` (a grep criterion over the diff) and the test uses only `git revert`, `worktree`, `rev-parse`, `log` and `update-ref` via `landCandidate`.
`landCandidate` is exported from queue.ts with its declaration unchanged, and every existing assertion in test/queue.test.ts still holds.

`culprits` holds exactly one culprit, naming the task and failing checks, on `reverted`, `revert-has-dependents` (task-7's `culprit` with `reproduced: true`, on the fixture where merge 3 depends on the culprit merge 2 by a plan edge, where `dependents` is `[task 3]`, and no other outcome sets `dependents`; answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-adee4fd6, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9c5f3805), `revert-not-applicable`, `revert-conflict`, `revert-red`, `integration-dirty`, `integration-moved`, and on `setup-failed` and `lock-timeout` raised while R is tested (one fixture each, neither needing a new seam: a `setupCmd` that exits 1 when the message of the commit checked out in its worktree carries a `Bs-Revert-Of` trailer, so the head run and every probe set up and only R's runs fail, with the result's `setup_failed` `{step: 'revert', commit: R}`; and criterion 4's lock-wait runner; answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-cb1c0515), and is empty on `green`, `not-reproduced`, `env-failure`, `red-at-base`, and on `setup-failed` and `lock-timeout` before a culprit (a setup failure or lock wait in the head run or in any of task-7's probes, before a culprit is named); the revert commit's message carries all four trailers.

Amended away (spec D4), fixture in this order: merge tasks 1-3 where merge 2 breaks a post-merge check; then a plan amendment drops the finished task 2 (the plan input is a v2 that omits it, as `draftNextVersion` does, with `plan-version-created` on the log); then `runPostMerge` -> `revert-not-applicable` with `reason: 'not-in-live-plan'` and task 2's culprit, no revert worktree created (step (3) never runs; the head run's and probes' scratch worktrees are task-7's, created and removed by it as on every outcome; answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329), the integration ref unchanged and no `wave-reverted` on the log. Without the amendment (the v1 plan input with task 2 live, and no `plan-version-created` for v2) the same repo gives `reverted`, so the two runs differ only by the amendment. Re-adding task 2 by a v3 amendment (its id in `liveTaskIds` again) makes the next call `reverted`, so the first way out the operator is offered works.

tasks.title: Ledger inputs: one project's events across lineages, qualified task ids, and the claims map
tasks.summary: Spec D6, AC8. A reader that gathers every session log for the epics under one specs dir across lineages, returns every kept event with the window bounds (no time filter; task-8 windows the numbers), keeps unattributed events, qualifies every task id, builds the task-to-claims map and sensitive globs, skips unreadable plans with a warning, and marks the result degraded on an unreadable session log.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/ledgerInputs.ts exporting `gatherLedgerInputs({stateDir, specsDir, sensitivePathsFile, now, windowDays})`. Layout: `specsDir` is the parent directory holding `<epic>/plan.json` and `<epic>/plan-v<n>.json`, as `--specs-dir` is on every existing verb. Epics: every `<epic>` directory there. Plans: the reader needs only `project`, `tasks`, and each task's `task_id` and `claims`; a plan file that does not parse or lacks those is skipped with a warning `{code: 'checks.plan-skipped', path, reason}` (no full plan validation). The project scope is the `project` of the readable plans; more than one distinct value throws `checks.mixed-projects`; no readable plan at all throws `checks.no-plans`. Events: every session in `stateDir` (events.ts `listSessionIds`, `readEvents`, `mergeSessionLogs`); a session `readEvents` cannot read adds `{code: 'checks.session-unreadable', path}` to the warnings and sets `degraded: true`. Keep an event when its epic (qualified `task_id`, `payload.epic_id`, or its session's single epic) is one of the epics, or when its session's lineage touches one of them. Do not filter by time: return `window: {from: now - windowDays, to: now}` beside the events, and task-8 applies it to the numbers only (spec D6). Qualify every kept event's task id with taskId.ts (`epicOfTaskId`, `qualifyTaskId`, `taskIdsMatch`): a qualified id as is; a bare id with its session's epic when the session or its lineage names exactly one epic; else `unattributed` (kept, never dropped). Claims: per qualified task id, the claims of its latest spec across the readable plan files, plus `task-added` records for follow-ups; a skipped plan's tasks get no entry, so task-8 counts them as sensitive. Sensitive globs: `loadSensitivePathsPolicy`. Returns `{events, window, taskIdOf, taskClaims, sensitiveGlobs, epics, project, sessionsRead, warnings, degraded}`. Read-only.
acceptance_criteria: test/ledgerInputs.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist): a fixture state dir with three sessions (two epics under the specs dir across two lineages, one epic elsewhere) yields every event of the two epics, in or out of the window, and none of the third, and `sessionsRead` is 3.

Events 31 and 400 days before `now` are both returned, and `window` is `[now - 30 days, now]` for a 30-day window. `taskClaims` takes a task's claims from its latest plan version, and a follow-up's from its `task-added` record.

A truncated plan file, and an old-schema plan missing a field the reader does not need, are handled differently: the truncated one is skipped with a `checks.plan-skipped` warning naming its path and its epic's events are still kept with no claims entries; the old-schema one is read. Plans naming two projects throw `checks.mixed-projects`; a specs dir with no readable plan throws `checks.no-plans`.
A session log with a non-JSON line yields `degraded: true` and a `checks.session-unreadable` warning naming the file; the other sessions' events are still returned.
Nothing in the state dir or specs dir changes (file mtimes and contents identical before and after).
