tasks.summary: Spec AC4-AC7, AC10, AC12. Ships `bs checks post-merge` (with automatic promotion, using the namespace-wide flags), `integration check --tier <tier|all|remaining>`, `epic close|verdict --checks`, and `worktree create --reopen --revert`.
tasks.objective: In cli.ts and usage.ts: (1) `bs checks post-merge --epic <id> --project <dir> --checks <file> --plan <plan.json> [--setup-cmd <cmd>] [--final] [--state-dir <dir>] [--now <iso>] --session <id> --plan-version <n> --causal-parent <event-id>` (flags mean what they mean in task-10; it takes no `--specs-dir`, because promotion needs no ledger and the plan comes from `--plan`, so run.md's line carries none; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-fd7db283) calls task-12's `runPostMerge` with the plan's tasks and edges and the effective checks, prints one JSON document with the outcome (and its `reason` when task-12 gives one, and task-12's `setup_failed` `{step, commit}` when the outcome is `setup-failed`, so the operator sees which run's setup failed and at which commit; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-4de860d8; task-12's `culprits` whenever it is non-empty; and task-12's `dependents` when the outcome is `revert-has-dependents`, so the operator deciding about a culprit with merged dependents sees the culprit and the tasks that depend on it; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9c5f3805), and exits 0 only for `green`, `reverted`, `no-checks-in-tier`, `no-new-merges` and `batch-not-ready`, else 1 (`revert-recorded` included, so the operator hears of it once). Exit 0 on the last three says that no batch is due, never that a tier passed: none of them runs a check or writes a record, so none certifies a check at close (task-6 reads records only) or releases a held task (`bs wave check` recomputes the hold from records), and the JSON names the outcome, never `green` (hard constraint 4, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3c48b247). For every entry in task-12's `culprits` (every outcome reached after the culprit is found, and a resumed write's culprit rebuilt from its trailers, spec D7), it calls task-9's `promoteAfterCatch` with that culprit. The JSON carries `promotions` exactly when `culprits` is non-empty: for each culprit in `culprits` order, the answers `promoteAfterCatch` returned for it, in their order, each with the culprit's task id added as `task`. That is one `{task, check, result, reason}` per failing check of each culprit, with `result` and `reason` as task-9 defines them (`promoted`, `declared-tier-wins`, `not-promoted` or `promotion-skipped`; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-e4d115dc). Promotion needs no ledger, and no answer changes the post-merge outcome or its exit code. The JSON also carries task-15's overlay report. (1b) `bs checks post-merge --held` with `--epic`, `--project`, `--checks`, `--plan` and `--session <id>`, `--state-dir <dir>` optional (`--plan-version` and `--causal-parent` are not required, since it writes nothing; without `--session` it exits 1 naming the flag before reading anything): read-only, it reads the `integration-check` records of that session's lineage (`readLineageEvents(--session)` against the store `--state-dir` names, else the default store), which is where `bs checks post-merge` and `bs integration check` write them under the epic session's envelope, a session started with `--continues` from it included, and prints `{held: [{task, waits_on}], uncertified_merges}` from task-7's `postMergeBase` and `heldByPostMerge`, creates no worktree, takes no lock, appends no event, and exits 0. (1c) `bs wave check` gains `--checks <file>` and `--project <dir>` (required together, and only with `--session`: `--checks` without `--session` exits 1 naming `--session`, because the hold is decided by records in the log): with them, it reads the same lineage events it already reads for in-flight tasks (`readLineageEvents(--session)`, `--state-dir` honoured), computes the same held map and calls task-17's `assertNotHeld` for every task it is asked to admit, so a held task is refused with `wave.held-by-post-merge` before anything is written; with `--session` and without `--checks`, on an epic for which task-5's `lastTieredRecordId(events, epicId)` over those lineage events is non-null (the same predicate task-6 uses to refuse a close without `--checks`, so the two refusals cannot disagree; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-250dd5ad), it refuses with `wave.checks-required`, so the hold cannot be skipped by leaving the flag off; on any other epic it behaves as on the base, and a call with no `--session` reads no log, exactly as on the base, which is why every playbook `wave check` line carries `--session` (task-11) (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-dc4b6bce; OQ-v2-1 (c), operator answer bs-check-tiers-run-2026-10-30#40). Document both in usage.ts. (2) `bs integration check --tier <pre-merge|post-merge|pre-release|all|remaining>` passes the tier. (3) `bs epic close` and `bs epic verdict` accept `--checks <file>` and pass it as task-6's `EpicVerdictInput.checks` (`DeclaredCheck[]`): one `{name, tier, checkSha256}` per effective entry in file order, `tier` the entry's effective tier and `checkSha256` task-1's `checkDigest(entry)`, so an empty file passes `[]`; without `--checks` they leave `checks` unset (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-1937e8e2). (4) In factory/orchestrator/src/worktree.ts add a reopen path, the new export `reopenTaskWorktree(projectDir: string, epicId: string, taskId: string, revertSha: string, opts?: {onScratch?: (scratchPath: string) => void}): TaskWorktree`. That is main's own return type of `createTaskWorktree`, `{worktreeDir, branch, epic, taskId}`, and `--reopen` prints that object exactly as `bs worktree create` prints it on main, with no key added. So wave.md step 9 and the queue read the reopened worktree as they read every other (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-5ecf58c3). `opts.onScratch` is a test seam, called once with the scratch worktree's absolute path right after it is created; the CLI never passes it (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-65a5c329). It is exposed as `bs worktree create <project-dir> <epic> <task-id> --reopen --revert <sha>` (spec D1): first, before any worktree is attached, any branch moves or any commit is made, refuse a dirty existing task worktree (`worktree.reopen-dirty`), a branch tip that is not an ancestor of the integration head (`worktree.reopen-not-ancestor`) and a `--revert` sha not on the integration branch (`worktree.reopen-revert-not-on-integration`). These are new `worktree.*` codes, each raised as a string literal the error-code scan reads. Main's `worktree.*` codes (`worktree.branch-delete-failed`, `worktree.default-branch-not-found`, `worktree.from-missing`, `worktree.remove-failed`, `worktree.reserved-task-id`) name none of these cases, and the near matches, `integration.dirty-tree` and `queue.adopt-not-on-integration`, belong to other verbs whose docs describe them (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-8a4bca7f). Each of these is read from refs and the existing worktree's status only, so a refusal leaves no worktree, ref or commit behind (the refusal-ordering sweep of f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329). Then build the commit before touching the task. In a scratch worktree detached at the integration head (under the `.wt/<project>/` root task-5 and task-12 use, named `scratch-<pid>-<uuid>`, task-5's scheme, so task-5's dead-pid sweep removes one a killed process left (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-71580e69), removed in a `finally`), run `git revert --no-edit <sha>`. If it conflicts: run `git revert --abort`, remove the scratch worktree, and refuse with `worktree.reopen-revert-conflict`, naming the sha and the conflicting paths. No task worktree is attached, no ref moves and no commit lands on any branch, so nothing is left behind (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-59c68d05). The operator recovers through the playbook, which hands the refusal over once (task-11, step 9). The culprit's change no longer applies cleanly on the current head, so the way out is a plan amendment that supersedes the task with one cut from the integration head, whose brief quotes the same `failing_checks` and `log_tail`. Otherwise the revert commit C, whose parent is the integration head, is the one new commit. Reuse the clean existing task worktree or attach one to the existing task branch without `-b`, and fast-forward the branch to C (its tip is an ancestor of the integration head, so of C); with no task branch, cut it at C. The branch only ever fast-forwards. In docs/specs/check-tiers-scope.md restore the `bs checks post-merge` code spans and write the shipped flags as invocations.
acceptance_criteria: test/postMergeCli.test.ts (write first; fails today because `checks post-merge` is not a verb): on task-12's fixture, `bs checks post-merge` prints `reverted` and exits 0; on the revert-conflict fixture prints `revert-conflict` and exits 1; on task-12's revert-has-dependents fixture (merge 3 depends on the culprit merge 2) prints `revert-has-dependents` with `culprits` naming task 2 and `dependents` equal to `[task 3]`, and exits 1 (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9c5f3805); on two merges with a task in flight and no dependent waiting prints `batch-not-ready`, exits 0, and creates no worktree; with a checks file holding no post-merge entry it prints `no-checks-in-tier`, exits 0, appends no event (the log's line count is unchanged) and creates no worktree, so nothing it did can certify a check (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3c48b247); on task-12's fixture with `--final` and a `--setup-cmd` that exits 1, it prints `setup-failed` with `setup_failed: {step: 'head', commit: <the integration head's full sha>}` and exits 1 (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-4de860d8).

With a culprit in `culprits`, an overlay-demoted failing check is promoted (`check-tier-promoted` on the log, overlay entry back to `pre-merge`, and the `promotions` entry `{task, check, result: 'promoted', reason: null}`) on `reverted`, on `revert-has-dependents`, and on a resumed `reverted` (a bs revert commit landed with task-7's builder, its red record and probe on the log, no `wave-reverted`) alike; with that red record absent from the log, the resumed `reverted` stands, nothing is promoted, and `promotions` holds `{task, check, result: 'promotion-skipped', reason: 'red-record-unreadable'}` for each failing check; a declared post-merge failing check gets `{task, check, result: 'declared-tier-wins', reason: null}`; with the overlay's location tracked by git, the outcome and exit code are unchanged and the entry is `{task, check, result: 'promotion-skipped', reason: 'checks.overlay-tracked'}`; on criterion 1's `batch-not-ready` fixture, whose `culprits` is empty, the JSON has no `promotions` key (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-e4d115dc).

`bs integration check --tier pre-release` writes a record with `tiers: ['pre-release']` and runs only that tier; `--tier remaining` after a passing post-merge record at the head runs no post-merge check; without `--tier` the verb runs the same checks with the same outcome and exit code as on the base, and it differs from the base in exactly two places (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-9e1584a7, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-87c40cb7). (a) The `integration-check` event payload it appends gains task-5's snake_case keys `tiers`, `tiers_present`, `tree_sha`, `not_run` and `environment`, plus `error_class` and `environment_evidence` only when a slept failure fires (`probe_of` never, since the CLI passes no `probeOf`). (b) The JSON it prints, `printJson` of the returned `IntegrationCheckRecord` (main's camelCase `epicId`, `branch`, `headSha`, `pass`, `results`, `eventId`, `ts`), gains task-5's camelCase record fields `tiers`, `tiersPresent`, `treeSha`, `notRun` and `environment`, plus `errorClass` and `environmentEvidence` only when a slept failure fires (`probeOf` never). On both sides each element of `results` is the same `CheckResult` and gains task-1's `cmd_sha256` and `check_sha256` (snake_case in both, being `CheckResult` fields). An existing test's exact assertion on either side may gain those keys and nothing else.

On a fixture where a bs revert landed and its task was superseded before `wave-reverted` was written, `bs checks post-merge` prints `revert-recorded` and exits 1 once; the next call proceeds to the normal flow.
`bs epic close --checks <file>` blocks with the tier named when only a post-merge record is current; without `--checks`, existing close tests are unchanged.

test/worktreeReopen.test.ts: after a revert landed, `--reopen --revert` leaves the task branch one commit ahead of the integration head with that commit's tree equal to the pre-revert head's; a dirty worktree, a non-ancestor tip and a sha off the integration branch are refused with `worktree.reopen-dirty`, `worktree.reopen-not-ancestor` and `worktree.reopen-revert-not-on-integration` respectively, each asserted by code (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-8a4bca7f), and each with nothing changed, and with no task worktree beforehand the last two are refused before one is attached (`git worktree list` and every ref identical before and after; answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329); with the branch deleted, the branch is cut from the head and gets the same commit. Conflicting revert (written first; fails today because the reopen path does not exist): a later merge on the integration branch edits the lines the revert would restore, so `git revert` conflicts. The call exits 1 with `worktree.reopen-revert-conflict`, naming the sha and the path. Afterwards `git worktree list`, every ref, the task branch's tip and the integration head are identical to before, no scratch worktree remains, and no worktree has a revert in progress (no `REVERT_HEAD` under the repository's git dir or any worktree's). Mutation: making the commit in the task worktree after the fast-forward fails this by name, because the branch has moved (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-59c68d05). `bs worktree create ... --reopen --revert` prints `{worktreeDir, branch, epic, taskId}`, the same keys a plain `bs worktree create` prints, with `worktreeDir` the absolute path of the reused or attached worktree (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-5ecf58c3). Scratch worktree, through `reopenTaskWorktree`'s `opts.onScratch` (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-71580e69, f-bs-check-tiers/integration-65a5c329): (1) In each case that reaches the revert build (the conflicting revert, the reused clean worktree, the attached worktree and the deleted branch), `onScratch` is called exactly once. Its path is `<root>/scratch-<pid>-<uuid>` with this process's pid, and the path is gone afterwards. (2) For the three early refusals (`worktree.reopen-dirty`, `worktree.reopen-not-ancestor`, `worktree.reopen-revert-not-on-integration`), `onScratch` is never called, and the root holds no `scratch-*` entry, before or after.
test/docCommands.test.ts passes on this tree with the restored spans; test/usage.test.ts still holds.

test/waveCheckHeld.test.ts (written first; fails today because neither `--held` nor `wave check --checks` exists), on task-7's repo builder with merges of A and B, a plan task C depending on A and an independent task D, a post-merge check declared, one epic session S and a temporary state dir T; every command below carries `--session S --state-dir T` (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-dc4b6bce). Before case (1) the test seeds S through test/helpers/cliHarness.ts's `taskStatusFixtures`, imported and not edited (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-a88f39ad): its `ingest` runs the real `bs plan ingest` of a plan holding A, B, C and D (C depending on A) into S and T, so `wave check` meets no `cli.plan-not-ingested` and C and D have `todo` rows; its `append` then writes one `wave-merged` for A and one for B, each with `task_ids` and the `merge_sha` of that task's merge commit on the builder's integration branch (the payload task-4's `emitWaveMergedWith` writes), so A and B fold to `completed` and `postMergeBase` reads them as uncertified merges. Then: (1) a held task refused by `wave check`: `bs checks post-merge --held` lists C waiting on A and nothing else, leaves no worktree, lock file or event behind, and `bs wave check <plan> C --checks <file> --project <dir>` exits 1 with `wave.held-by-post-merge` naming C and A, writing no event; (2) an independent task admitted while a batch runs: with the batch due and its post-merge record not yet written, `bs wave check <plan> D --checks <file> --project <dir>` admits D; (3) a held task admitted after proceed: `bs checks post-merge` with the envelope `--session S --plan-version <n> --causal-parent <id> --state-dir T` returns `green` and writes its record into S's log, where the real flow writes it; then `--held` lists nothing and `bs wave check` admits C; the same holds when the green record is written under a session that continues S (`bs session start --continues S`), because the read is the lineage. Also: `--held` and `bs wave check --checks` without `--session` exit 1 naming `--session` and read nothing; `bs wave check --session S` without `--checks` on that log exits 1 with `wave.checks-required`, and so does a log whose only tiered record is a pre-release-only record (`tiers_present: ['pre-merge', 'pre-release']`) or a probe, while a log of records with `tiers_present: ['pre-merge']` only behaves as on the base (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-250dd5ad); on a project with no post-merge entry nothing is held; every existing `wave check` test passes unchanged (OQ-v2-1 (c), operator answer bs-check-tiers-run-2026-10-30#40).

Diff check (AC13), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff --no-renames <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout (for example a `timeout_ms` line that only validates or passes through an existing value). An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

functional_clauses: The CLI only parses flags and calls library functions; bisect, revert, promotion and fold logic stay in their modules.
`--reopen` only fast-forwards and appends a commit; it never resets, rebases or forces a branch.
Exit 0 only for the five proceed outcomes; every other outcome exits 1 with the outcome named.
`bs checks post-merge --held` is read-only; `bs wave check` refuses through task-17's `assertNotHeld` over task-7's `heldByPostMerge`, never a second rule.
nonfunctional_clauses: Read factory/specs/active/bs-check-tiers/epic-spec.md before starting, in full, including Decisions D1-D7. Do not edit it: it sits outside every task's claims. Put one Progress line for it in the result `notes` (what changed, and anything a later task must know); the epic session copies it in at merge.

Base: main at c13458d8 or later, where bs-optimize (#501), the CI quick wins (#502), bs-gate-bounce (#510) and the diff-cap fix (#511) have all merged. The upstream exports this epic consumes, as they are on that base: `isHeavyCheck`, `heavyChildEnv` and `RunOptions.heavyLock` (testgate.ts); `withHeavyLock`, which re-enters a held lock only when its env's `BS_HEAVY_LOCK_TOKEN` equals the holder's token (heavyLock.ts); `bs heavy run`; the clock evidence `RunResult.environment`, a `CheckEnvironment[]` index-parallel to `results` (one entry per result: `name`, `window: 'command' | 'none'`, `wall_ms`, `monotonic_ms`, `clock_gap_ms`, loads, `cpus`), which gate.ts writes as `testgate-result.payload.environment` beside `results`; and the sleep classifier `sleptDuringCheck(entry)` with `SLEEP_GAP_MS` (testgate.ts). There is no `CheckResult.environment`: a result never carries its own evidence. If one of these is missing on the base, stop and report it in `notes`; never re-implement it. (Answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-ec6b37dd.)

Diff budget (#511): `diff_lines` caps the non-test lines of the diff only; test files and fixtures (`diffstat.ts` `isTestDiffPath`) are measured apart as `testLines` and never capped. Size nothing down to fit the cap by thinning a test.
TDD: write the named failing test first, run it and watch it fail for the stated reason, then implement until it passes. Record the failing run's assertion message in `notes`.

Before hand-back run, in the foreground and in full: `pnpm run build`, root `pnpm run test` (the whole suite, never a scoped file), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test` and `pnpm exec biome check .` from the repo root (the whole repo, never a scoped path); report each exit code and the tail of each output. Run the full suite through `bs heavy run` so it takes the machine's heavy lock.
Also run `bash scripts/check.sh` and read the tail of its output, not only its exit code; name every step it printed as SKIP.

Weaken nothing: add no `.skip`, `.only`, `.todo`, `.fails`, `retry`, quarantine list or flaky marker; raise no `testTimeout`, `hookTimeout`, `timeout_ms`, `waitForLines` default, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` or any other timeout; remove, loosen or reorder no existing assertion, check, gate stage, grader, judge, review round or verifier. An existing exact-payload assertion may gain this task's new fields and nothing else.

Open source, any stack: no other project's name, no client code and no absolute home-directory path (`/Users/...`, `/home/...`) in any committed file, fixtures included. No per-stack tier default anywhere; nothing may require GitHub Actions; `bs new` keeps scaffolding no `checks.json`.
Add no runtime or dev dependency.
For each new branch of logic, run a mutation check (disable it, run the new test file, see a named test fail, restore) and list the results in `notes`.
Do not edit anything under factory/policies/.
Do not edit CHANGELOG.md: task-11 is its sole owner in this epic. Put a one-paragraph, user-facing description of this change under `notes` in the result so task-11 can write the Unreleased entry.

keeps_exports promise on worktree.ts: the reopen path is new exports only; `createTaskWorktree`, `removeTaskWorktree`, `taskBranchName`, `integrationBranchName` and every other existing export keep their declarations. Verified post-run by `bs claims impact`.

tasks.title: The learned-tier overlay: location, validity, one writer at a time, crash order, reconcile, report
tasks.summary: Spec D8, AC9, AC10. A bs-owned, git-excluded overlay at `<project-root>/.blacksmith/check-tiers.json` with named validity rules, a lock and revision check for every write, refusal of tracked, un-excludable and non-git locations, reconciliation with the log, and one report precedence; the project's checks file is never written.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/tierOverlay.ts exporting: `overlayPath(dir)` (the main worktree of the repository holding `dir`, from `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, then `.blacksmith/check-tiers.json`; null outside a git repository); `readOverlay(dir)` (absent -> empty at revision 0; invalid per spec D8's rules -> `{unreadable: <first violation>}`, never a throw); `overlayWritable(dir)` (`ok`, or the reason: `not-a-repo`, `tracked` (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`), `unreadable`); `withOverlayLock(dir, fn, opts)` (never called when `overlayPath(dir)` is null: task-9's apply and task-10's proposals check first and answer `not-a-repo` without locking, task-9's promotion reaches the lock only for a check with an overlay tier, which no directory outside a git repository has, and a call made anyway throws `checks.overlay-not-a-repo` before creating anything; it is called only by a caller that may write: task-9's apply, which validates under the lock and may then refuse; task-9's promotion, once it will write; and task-10's proposals, once something is owed. So it creates `.blacksmith/` when absent; a call that ends without a write may leave that empty directory, which git does not track, and never a lock file (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329), then creates `check-tiers.lock` beside the overlay with `O_EXCL`, its whole content the holder's pid in decimal followed by one newline; breaks a lock whose pid is dead (heavyLock.ts `pidIsAlive`) and never one whose pid is alive, this process's own included, so a second call in the holder's process waits like any other; waits up to `opts.waitMs`, polling every `OVERLAY_LOCK_POLL_MS = 100` ms (a module constant), then throws `checks.overlay-busy`; always releases (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-97b65272)). `opts.waitMs` defaults to the exported constant `OVERLAY_LOCK_WAIT_MS = 30000`, commented with its reason: every holder keeps the lock for one reconcile plus one atomic overlay write and a few event appends, milliseconds on a quiet machine and seconds on a loaded one, so 30 s outlasts any live holder and only a hung one makes a waiter give up; a lock left by a dead pid is broken at once and never waited on (raised by the planner, no finding id). The wait is asynchronous and polls on timers (`setTimeout`), never a busy loop or a synchronous sleep. When the wait expires, the waiter throws `checks.overlay-busy` naming the holder's pid and the wait in ms, and writes nothing: `fn` never runs, the overlay and the event log are untouched, the holder's lock file is left as it is, and the waiter leaves no lock file of its own. Production callers pass no `waitMs` and rely on this default without restating its value: task-9's apply and promotion, and task-10's proposals. Only this task's own tests pass one; `writeOverlay(dir, {entries, expectedRevision}, opts)` (must run inside the lock; refuses `checks.overlay-not-a-repo`, `checks.overlay-tracked`, `checks.overlay-unreadable`, and `checks.overlay-moved` when the file's revision is not `expectedRevision`; writes revision + 1 atomically via a temp sibling and rename, with `opts.beforeRename` as the test seam for an injected crash; creates `.blacksmith/` when absent; calls workroot.ts `excludeFromGit`, which this task exports without other change, and proceeds only on `added` or `already-ignored`, else refuses `checks.overlay-exclude-failed` or `checks.overlay-tracked` and leaves no overlay written); `resolveEffectiveTiers(checks, overlay)` (per entry: declared `tier` -> `declared`; else an overlay entry with the same name and `commandDigest(cmd)` -> `overlay`; else `pre-merge`/`default`; an unreadable or absent overlay resolves every undeclared entry to `pre-merge`/`default`); `overlayReport(checks, overlay)` (spec D8's precedence: no entry with that name -> `orphaned`; that entry declares a tier -> `shadowed`, also when its command changed; digest differs -> `orphaned`; else `active`); `overlayOwes(overlay, events)` (pure: the approved `check-tier-decided` and `check-tier-promoted` tiers the overlay lacks and the `pending_event`s still owed; empty for an absent overlay when the log holds no approved decision); and `reconcileOverlay(dir, events, ctx, opts)` (inside the lock, re-reading the overlay there and writing exactly what `overlayOwes` reports: entries the approved `check-tier-decided` and `check-tier-promoted` events imply but the overlay lacks are written; a `pending_event` still owed is appended through `appendEvent` exactly as stored and cleared; nothing else changes). An entry's `pending_event`, when present, is an object with exactly `event_type` (the string `check-tier-promoted`) and an object `payload`; anything else makes the overlay unreadable. tierOverlay.ts writes no event type of its own: it recognises `check-tier-decided` and `check-tier-promoted` by comparing `event_type` strings and appends only the stored `pending_event`, so no `event_type:` property in it names a literal or constant, and it adds nothing to taxonomy.yml (task-9, which writes the three `check-tier-*` names, declares them).
acceptance_criteria: test/tierOverlay.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist): from a task worktree of a temp repo and from its main clone, `overlayPath` returns the same file under the main clone's `.blacksmith/`; in a plain directory outside any repository it returns null, `resolveEffectiveTiers` gives every undeclared entry `pre-merge`, and `writeOverlay` refuses `checks.overlay-not-a-repo`.

Validity: each of these makes `readOverlay` return `unreadable` naming the rule: a non-object; `version` 2; a negative `revision`; an empty `check`; a 63-hex `cmd_sha256`; `tier` `"later"`; an unknown key; a `pending_event` with a key other than `event_type` and `payload`; two entries with the same `check` and `cmd_sha256`. A valid file reads back deep-equal.

Report precedence: for one overlay entry `e2e`, the check absent from the file -> `orphaned`; present and declaring a tier -> `shadowed`, also with its command edited; present, undeclared, command edited -> `orphaned`; present, undeclared, same command -> `active`, and `resolveEffectiveTiers` gives it the overlay tier with source `overlay`.

Exclusion: `writeOverlay` in a fresh repo leaves `git status --porcelain` empty in the main clone and adds one line to `.git/info/exclude` (no tracked `.gitignore` changes); with `.blacksmith/check-tiers.json` committed to the repo it refuses `checks.overlay-tracked` and the file is unchanged; with `.git/info/exclude` made read-only (exclude returns `failed`) it refuses `checks.overlay-exclude-failed` and writes no overlay.

One writer: two writers started together under `withOverlayLock`, each adding a different entry after reading, both succeed in turn and the file holds both entries; a write with a stale `expectedRevision` refuses `checks.overlay-moved`; a lock file the test writes in the stated format with a pid known not to be alive is broken; a lock held through a first `withOverlayLock` call in this process makes a second call throw `checks.overlay-busy` after `waitMs`. Default wait (raised by the planner, no finding id), written first; it fails today because the constant does not exist: (1) `OVERLAY_LOCK_WAIT_MS` is exported and equals 30000. (2) The test holds the lock through a first `withOverlayLock` call in this process, whose `fn` waits on a promise the test settles at the end, never by writing `check-tiers.lock` itself, and makes a second call with `waitMs` omitted, under vitest fake timers (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-97b65272). The call is still pending after `OVERLAY_LOCK_WAIT_MS - 1` ms. Once the clock passes `OVERLAY_LOCK_WAIT_MS`, it rejects with `checks.overlay-busy` naming the holder's pid. (3) `fn` never ran; the overlay's bytes, the event log's line count and the holder's lock file are unchanged; no lock file of the waiter's exists. (4) A dead-pid lock file, written by the test in the stated format, is broken with no wait. (5) Mutation: a default of 0, or none (waiting forever), fails this by name.

Crash: `opts.beforeRename` throwing leaves the previous overlay byte-identical and no temp sibling behind after the next successful write. `reconcileOverlay` writes the tier of an approved `check-tier-decided` missing from the overlay, appends the `check-tier-promoted` held in a `pending_event` exactly once, and is a no-op on a consistent pair.
The project's checks file is never written: every exported function run against a temp repo whose checks file is mode 0444 leaves that file's bytes and mtime unchanged and raises no permission error.

No write, no lock: in a plain directory outside any repository `withOverlayLock` throws `checks.overlay-not-a-repo` and creates nothing (directory listing identical before and after); in a repo with no `.blacksmith/`, `overlayOwes` of the absent overlay and a log with no approved decision is empty, and the first `withOverlayLock` creates `.blacksmith/` for its lock and leaves no lock file after `fn` returns or throws. `overlayOwes` names a missing approved entry and an owed `pending_event`, and `reconcileOverlay` writes exactly those.

tasks.summary: Spec D4, AC6. tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/postMergeResume.ts exporting `resumeLandedReverts(input, ctx, opts)`. Invalid trailers -> `record-only` with reason `invalid-trailers`; a task id the lineage does not know -> `unknown-task`. Otherwise call task-2's `waveRevertBlocker` with `revertSha`, a git `isAncestor` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) and `liveTaskIds`: null -> `recordWaveReverted` with `disposition: bounce`, `resumed: true`, `failing_checks` from the trailer, the log tail and evidence ids from the red record when it can be read (`evidence: 'record'`), else the trailer's checks and the red record id only (`evidence: 'trailers-only'`); a reason -> `record-only` with that reason and whatever evidence can be read (`evidence: 'unreadable'` with empty lists when none). Each write whose trailers are valid and whose task is known and merged (every reason except `invalid-trailers`, `unknown-task` and `not-merged`) also yields `culprit`, rebuilt from the trailers in task-12's shape: `{task: <Bs-Task, qualified>, merge_sha: <Bs-Revert-Of>, failing_checks: <Bs-Failing-Checks>, red_record_event_id: <Bs-Red-Record>, reproduced: true}`. `reproduced: true` holds because task-12 builds a bs revert commit only after task-7 returned `culprit-found` (spec D4); whether each check's own failure was env or not-run is read later from the red record by task-9's promotion, never assumed here. Return `{outcome, resumed, wrote: [{task, revert_sha, disposition, reason?, culprit?}]}`: outcome `reverted` with `resumed: true` when every write was a bounce, `revert-recorded` when any was record-only, `nothing-to-resume` (`resumed: false`) when none was missing. It never moves a ref. Its fixtures are built inside test/postMergeResume.test.ts with the repo builder task-7 exports from test/helpers/integrationRepo.ts (imported, not edited).
acceptance_criteria: test/postMergeResume.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist), with a bs revert commit landed and no `wave-reverted`: the task still completed -> one `wave-reverted` with `disposition: bounce`, return `{outcome: 'reverted', resumed: true}`, and the task folds to `todo`.

Every bad trailer value is written through the trailer parameters of task-7's builder, never by a hand-made commit.
Mislabel guard: the task's original `wave-merged` carries the `merge_sha` R reverts; the resume writes a `bounce`, never `re-merged`.

Unreadable evidence: with the red record named by `Bs-Red-Record` absent from the log, a bounceable task gets a `bounce` with `evidence: 'trailers-only'` and `failing_checks` from the trailer; a superseded one gets a `record-only` with `evidence: 'unreadable'`; neither write is refused.

No repetition: after any exit, a second call returns `nothing-to-resume` and writes nothing. A bs revert commit that is itself the latest certified commit, and one older than the base, are both found.
The integration ref and the clone's branch, index and tree are byte-identical before and after every fixture.

tasks.title: A bounced revert reopens the task everywhere the lifecycle is read
tasks.summary: Spec D1, AC7. The projector, finishedInLog and reinstatementBlocker treat a `bounce` wave-reverted as no merge, so goal-check, amend, readiness, wave next and admission all see the task as open; `record-only` changes nothing.
tasks.objective: A task is reverted when its latest `wave-merged` is followed by a `wave-reverted` with `disposition: 'bounce'` naming it (match the event type and payload by their strings, as the projector's other arms do, so this task imports nothing from task-2's revert.ts); a `record-only` event never reopens anything. Apply that rule in: db/projector.ts `foldTasks` (`completed` -> `todo`, clearing whatever terminal bookkeeping a later `wave-merged` needs; read schema.ts's `terminalAt` comment and keep its rule; other statuses untouched); taskLifecycle.ts `finishedInLog` (a reverted task is not finished, so `creditableTaskIds`, `markFinishedFromLog`/`draftNextVersion`, specChange.ts and spec.ts all see it open without edits of their own) and `reinstatementBlocker` (a reverted merge is no merge). Change waveNext.ts or admission.ts only where a test shows the reverted row is not offered or admitted. A task the live plan no longer holds is never bounced: a plan amendment drops a finished task from v(n+1) (plan.ts `draftNextVersion`), so task-2's `waveRevertBlocker` returns `not-in-live-plan` for it, task-12 builds no revert, and task-16 records an already-landed one `record-only` (spec D4). Every `bounce` this task reads therefore names a task the live plan holds, and it needs no way back for a dropped one. The new arm makes `projectTasks` compare one more event type, so add `'wave-reverted'` to db/foldPredicates.ts `TASK_TYPES`: test/db/foldPredicates.test.ts walks `projectTasks` and every function it calls and fails any compared type the tasks predicate rejects on an empty payload. Compare against a string literal or a module-level `const` so that guard can resolve the operand, and change nothing else in foldPredicates.ts (its only importer is projector.ts, which this task also claims; no other task claims either file). For OQ-v2-1 (c) (operator answer bs-check-tiers-run-2026-10-30#40), add to admission.ts a pure export beside `assertNotInFlight`: `assertNotHeld(taskId, held)`, where `held` maps a task id to the merged task ids it waits on (task-7's `heldByPostMerge`, computed and passed in by `bs wave check`, task-14), throwing a new `HeldByPostMergeError` with code `wave.held-by-post-merge` naming the task and those merges; admission.ts reads no integration record and imports nothing from task-5 or task-7, so this task keeps its wave.
acceptance_criteria: test/waveReverted.test.ts (write first; fails today because the projector ignores `wave-reverted` and the row stays `completed`): after `wave-merged` then a `bounce` `wave-reverted` for task T (raw events in the fixture), `foldTasks` gives T `todo`; a second `wave-merged` gives `completed` again.

After the bounce: `finishedInLog` omits T; `creditableTaskIds` does not credit T; `markFinishedFromLog` then `draftNextVersion` keeps T live (not completed, not dropped) in the drafted next version; the epic readiness check lists T as not terminal-OK; `computeNextWave` with the log's status map offers T; `inFlightTasks` does not count T in flight. After a second `wave-merged` each of these reads T as finished again.

A `record-only` `wave-reverted` for a completed task and for a superseded task changes none of these readers. Nor does one with `reason: 'not-in-live-plan'`, in this order: `wave-merged` for T, a `plan-version-created` whose v2 omits T (as `draftNextVersion` drafts it), then the `record-only` event; `finishedInLog` still lists T, `creditableTaskIds` still credits it through its earlier-version rule, and `draftNextVersion` of v2 does not bring T back.
`reinstatementBlocker` for a superseded task whose only merge was bounced reports the missing merge, as for a task that never merged.
Every existing assertion in the projector, taskLifecycle, goal-check, spec-change, waveNext, admission and reinstate tests still holds.

test/db/foldPredicates.test.ts passes with `'wave-reverted'` in `TASK_TYPES`; with that one entry removed it fails by name (`wave-reverted (compared in projectTasks in db/projector.ts)` or the taskLifecycle.ts function it calls). The mutation run's failing line is in `notes`.

Mutation: returning without the check fails this test by name (OQ-v2-1 (c), operator answer bs-check-tiers-run-2026-10-30#40).

An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

Only `completed` rows reopen; superseded, waived, failed and escalated tasks are never reopened, and `record-only` reopens nothing.

tasks.title: What `bs new` scaffolds carries the CI flow and the tiers
tasks.summary: Factory-level. Spec AC15, AC13, hard constraints 1 and 4. The scaffold gets one gate script run the same way locally and in CI, CI jobs per tier with PR-scoped cancel-in-progress (a tier with nothing to run is skipped, never passed), and, in the `ui` layer, a sharded e2e workflow on ci.yml's events with a cached browser and a non-fatal screenshot upload that a detect job keeps dormant until the project has a `test:e2e` script.
tasks.objective: Carry this repo's CI flow (#502, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `scripts/check.sh`) into what `bs new` scaffolds, so it reaches every user in the next release (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-a46729fa), inside hard constraint 1 and AC13: no per-stack tier default, `bs new` still scaffolds no `checks.json`, and the project works without GitHub Actions. (1) New `factory/scaffold/base/scripts/check.mjs`, Node built-ins only, run as `pnpm run check` (add the script to factory/scaffold/base/package.json): `node scripts/check.mjs [--tier pre-merge|post-merge|pre-release|all] [--list] [--ci]`, `--tier` defaulting to `all`; one leading `--` argument is dropped before parsing, because pnpm 9 forwards it to the script (`pnpm run check -- --tier pre-merge` hands node `['--', '--tier', 'pre-merge']`) (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-541a89dd). Without a `checks.json` at the project root it runs the scaffold's own gates, in TOOLCHAIN_STEPS order without the install (`pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test`, `pnpm run test:coverage`, `pnpm run build`), as an unlabelled list, so every one is pre-merge (spec Goal 1).
